## 2026-11-23: semantic application codebase replaces universal goal/report routing

Owner requested all six migration steps across the full VibeStudio corpus.
The shared specialist hierarchy is retained; 116 typed entry kinds across 27
roots replace universal `runUserGoal` admission. All 2,327 goal identities/hashes,
source groups and splits are unchanged (1,748 train/579 test; 114 entry programs
used). Application inputs and results are bound to exact capture source, ordered
named arguments and original JavaScript JSON bytes. The native trajectory IR
and call graph remain the training representation.

Removed gratuitous read-count, execution-order, generic final-report and route
constraints across the templates. Actual requested outcomes, required answers,
protected scope and claimed evidence remain verified. Runtime authorized rereads
and concurrent reads were fixed at shared bindings, including Drive cursor-chain
reconciliation. Authored ambient declarations now reach the production compiler
without adding runtime authority. All 116 entries compile; Host120, SST32,
shared-library/provider30 and loader61 focused tests passed; main quick check
passed after the ordinary merge with ongoing expert-iteration work.

Failed captures remain immutable. Evidence-bound recovery exposed ten prior
captures/42 decisions without relabeling whole tasks as successful. Incorrect
optional root return generations remain observed but carry no supervised target;
when effects and a false return share one completion, no fabricated token split
is introduced. Source branches were integrated to each template main, Host main
and Natlang main. The complete workspace release and live cutover use these
committed sources, preserving the old release as rollback. Recovery export and
student reasoning fill feed the existing expert-iteration pipeline; DGX jobs queue
rather than violate the 15GB diagnostic reserve or interrupt training.

No held gain is claimed by source compilation or verifier tests. Observe actual
entry breadth, nested functions, depth, branching and composition in new captures;
judge learned capability with the paired held evaluation already used by training.

### 2026-11-23: Retry teacher goals against the repaired release

The Vibestudio campaign previously applied its two-attempt limit across every historical harness release. Repaired outcomes therefore left failed goals permanently exhausted. Attempt accounting now defaults to the validated release-manifest SHA as its epoch, retaining cumulative telemetry and every historical verified success. New wave plans and execution subsets carry immutable release/catalog/driver/Host provenance; old receipts and plans remain untouched, and unfinished historical captures can be archived without running their old jobs under a different release. `--attempt-epoch` provides an explicit accounting override. This changes campaign bookkeeping, not semantic outcome requirements or the existing task selection policy. Targeted tests use mocked collection; no new generation was launched. Mechanism inventory: `VIBESTUDIO_ATTEMPT_EPOCHS.md`.

## 2026-11-23 B5: the decision objective in expert-iteration SFT (WS5 O3)

- **Change (default on, opt-out `exp0_sft --no-decision-objective`).** A call on a decision readout's surface (no
  tools, last message the readout's request, reply one of the offered JSON values) is a scored choice, not a sampled
  reply. `sft_sources build` (`render_candidate`/`admit` -> `render_decision`) now carries each such row's option set:
  the closed continuation of every option rendered by the scorer's own `serve.native_learning.decision_items` (what the
  Python engine and the SGLang actor score), the label (the verified trajectory's choice, own and teacher) and the
  option texts. `exp0_sft.chains_of` makes each decision its own chain; `decision_backward` trains
  `common.decision_objective.decision_loss` (logLoss, the native-graph trainer's objective) over the options' full-softmax
  sequence log-probabilities, one target unit of loss mass per decision, in every step (Ambient TM steps included).
  The plain row stays in the chain, so the opt-out (and an older learner reading a new mix) trains the token CE of the
  chosen reply as before. A `--resume` keeps the setting its learner state trained with (it changes the step list).
  `lower_sft_sources.py` no longer drops decision rows: they become decision chains (Neuralese-importing ones are
  skipped and counted). Why: the runtime's answer and confidence are softmax(s); the token CE of the chosen reply can
  neither lower a wrongly preferred option nor ignore the shared format tokens.
- **Teacher distributions:** none of our teacher endpoints returns prompt log-probabilities (the replay declines
  scoring, `ReplayEpisode.answer`), so teacher decisions train on their label. A `probabilities` target is supported
  by the learner and by `lower_sft_sources` for when one does.
- **Verified.** 431/431 own decision captures of sft-v9's collection (SGLang actor) equal the build rendering byte for
  byte (prompt ids, every option continuation, label = `decision_sample.chosen`); 196/196 replayed decision rows equal a
  capture; 8 captures with Neuralese prompts never reach the build (replay skips them). In sft-v9's mix the objective
  covers 307 own and 3,982 teacher decision rows (~5.5M extra forward tokens per epoch against 292M, 1.9%). Tests:
  `tests/neuralese/test_sft_decision_objective.py` (the loss equals the served scores' softmax CE on an engine
  fixture; gradient equals the explicit option CE; build rendering carries options into chains and `build.json`
  `mix.decisions`; lowered graph decisions).
- **Reports.** `build.json`: `stats.<source>.decision_rows/decision_options/decision_surface_not_carried:*` and
  `mix.decisions`; `train.log`: `decision_objective` at start, per step `decisions`, `decision_ce`,
  `decision_accuracy`, `decision_loss_share`, and `val_decision_ce:*`/`val_decision_accuracy:*` for validation sets
  holding decisions.

## 2026-11-23 02:30 Memetic groups in expert-iteration collection; every guided memetic evaluation had failed (B15; e89558c2b)

Brief B15 (`plans/semantic-fp/09_FIRST_BATCH.md`): expert-iteration collection forced `--memetic-share 0`. Owner
2026-11-18: memetic stays on; the gap is telemetry, not a gate.

  the bare state id; `ts-host/src/guidance/program.ts` (since 214f3ad2a, 2026-10-31) accepts only the native-state
  sentinel `<id>`. Every guided nested run exited in 0.6 s with "invalid
  natlang.memetic-program-guidance/1 binding" (grpo-v4 run2: 84 in one shared collector log; the 20 recorded bindings
  all fail under today's runtime). The evaluator scored those collections (0 of 12 scored) as success 0, so
  `baseline-query-default` was 0 in every group and each supervisor's guided support evaluation read 0. The grpo-v4
  `memetic_groups` gap (15 groups, all <= 0) measured a broken channel, not memetic learning: any change set holding
  guidance scored 0 on support and query (file changes such as instruction patches and skills did run), and the GRPO
  memetic advantages trained on those scores. Fixed: the sentinel
  (`NATIVE_SENTINEL_OPEN/CLOSE`); an evaluation with no scored run reports `success: None` (the anchor ignores it, the
  supervisor's `evaluate` answers that it is not counted against the budget, a group whose support runs all failed is
  not admitted, a committed set whose query runs all failed leaves the episode unmeasured); the shared collector
  writes an invocation's error into the invocation's own log (`run_bonsai_queue.SharedChild`; it reached only the
  server log, which hid this). MODEL_FACING_CHANGES entry.
- **Memetic groups in collection by default.** `expert_iteration.MEMETIC_SHARE = 0.02` on `collect`, `cycle` and
  `async-drive` (`--memetic-share 0` opts out; `collect_command` passes it), tasks from the role `grpo-memetic-tasks`.
  At most `MEMETIC_MAX_GROUPS = 2` memetic groups run at once (each sample runs ~30 nested rollouts beside its slot:
  bounded actor and host-memory load), and none starts when its wall clock (`world.case_seconds`, 7200 s) no longer
  fits before the collection deadline (the collection would wait for it). No JOLT+ teacher attempts of a memetic group
  (its reward is graded against its anchor; the `== 1.0` rule made every memetic group "failing").
- **Success and the SFT mix.** `task_rollouts.memetic_success`: committed, not leak-refused, workspace scored, and
  quality (query success minus evaluation cost) > anchor (best of no change / mechanical default on the same query
  worlds and seeds): the condition under which GRPO gives a positive advantage. Rollout and rewards rows carry
  `memetic_success`; `expert_iteration.group_outcomes` (frontier, select) and `sft_sources extract` read it, so a
  memetic success enters as `rl-own`. Targets are the supervisor's own calls (its replies, including the guidance text
  it writes through `workspace.propose`); prompts, workspace evidence and tool outputs are zero-weight context; the
  nested runs of the guided program live under the group's `memetic/evals/` and are never extracted.
- **Separate invocations and leaks.** Support worlds are the supervisor's evidence and evaluations; query worlds score
  the commit and are never shown (`memetic_tasks.split`, one world per related component). `leaked_answers` refuses a
  commit reproducing a query answer (>= 6 chars) verbatim. New: the collector leaves out memetic rows any of whose
  support/query worlds is in the held closure of `--held-manifest`/`--exclude-manifest` (`grpo.memetic_rows_held_free`;
  the 11-18 set was built against held-v3, a later held set must also apply), and the SFT build drops a memetic row
  whose `curriculum.world_ids` meet the held ids. B1 (held-v4): route `memetic_rows_held_free` through
  `training_exclusion_ids` when it lands.
- **Replay.** `sft_sources replay` re-runs a memetic success from its recorded evaluations: the group's spec copied
  with `recorded_only` (prepared evidence and every `evals/*/summary.json`, by name), so the replayed supervisor sees
  the same evidence and scores, and any evaluation the recording lacks fails the replay instead of sampling a model;
  a spec with `refine` is refused. Replayed success is re-derived (`memetic_success`) from the replayed score.

## 2026-11-23 05:30 Malleable code through a transaction: protected judges, recorded revisions, adopt-call (semantic-FP B8, WS1 L3)

Decision (WS1 L3, kept): `edit_code` stays on wherever a call owns code; what judges the call is protected, and a good
edit becomes a proposal the program can adopt instead of dying with the run. The default stays `allow`.
- **Protected items.** New frontmatter `protect: [path, ...]` (paths from the function's companion folder; extension
  optional; a subfolder protects everything in it). `edit_code` refuses (code `protected`, one teaching sentence, WS4 §8
  text) the protected items of the executing function and of every function in its codebase tree, the program's
  `types.ts`, and an edit that changes any `protect:` list (so a nested function cannot unprotect its verifier). An
  entry that names no item is a load error. Services were already refused as external (unchanged text).
  `ensures:` checks (L7, B12) are not on main yet: when they land, their named items join `treeProtectedSources`
  (`runtime/loader.ts`), the one place protection is computed.
- **Revisions are recorded.** Each committed edit emits a `code_revision` trace event (item, source, revision, hashes,
  the find/replace patch, the edited text); a call that ends `done` records them as `code_revisions` in its call record
  (`after` is a blob ref linked against eviction). `natlang traces show` lists them; the dashboard trace page shows them
  with **Adopt this fix** (job kind `adopt-call`).
- **Adoption is a Folder transaction.** `natlang improve adopt-call CALL [--into DIR] [--dry-run] [--untested]` takes the
  last revision of each source, refuses a stale checkout (file hash must equal the text the call edited), refuses any
  change to `types.ts`, protected items or `protect:` lists, materializes the proposal in a temp copy, runs `natlang
  check` and `natlang test` there (the real CLI, as subprocesses), and installs through `improvement/adoption.ts`
  `adoptSource` (adoption record first, atomic install). `natlang improve rollback RECORD` restores the exact bytes. A
  program with no saved examples is refused unless `--untested` (adopt on check alone): adopting untested model edits
  silently would make the gate decorative.
- **Stale comment fixed** (`native/runtime.ts`: "edit_code is offered to every call"; it is offered only where
  `codeEditable()` holds, `agent.ts` toolsScope).
- **Inventory.** Changed: `runtime/loader.ts` (key, validation, resolution helpers), `runtime/callable.ts`,
  `runtime/kernel.ts` (definition plumbing), `native/values.ts` (`protectedSources`), `native/runtime.ts` (refusals,
  event), `calls/{types,recorder,store-core,expanded,trace-view}.ts`, `improvement/adopt-call.ts`, `cli/improvement.ts`,
  `cli/main.ts`, `dashboard/server.ts`, `dashboard/{run-host.js,pages/traces.js}`, spec SPEC/ERRORS, skill SKILL.md and
  `references/language.md`, MODEL_FACING_CHANGES. Not changed, with reason:
  - Engines (managed llama-server, wllama, Python native, SGLang): edit_code runs in ts-host (`native/runtime.ts`
    `functionTool`); engines see only the tool schemas, which are unchanged (`native/agent.ts` toolsScope, edit_code
    still offered under `session.codeEditable()`), and the refusal text as an observation.
  - Browser runtime: shares `native/runtime.ts` and `runtime/loader.ts`, so protection applies there too; adopt-call is
    Node-only (it installs files in a checkout; `improvement/adoption.ts` is `node:fs`).
  - `ProgramView` (`adaptation/program-view.ts`): unchanged; revisions stay run-scoped there, recording reads the event.
  - Learner, held eval, collectors, Python renderers of recorded prompts: they replay recorded messages; no message
    changed except the refusal observation, and the new trace event kind is not a message. Held and EI collection pass
    `codeEdits: 'deny'` already (WS1 L3 v2 fact).
  - Authored-task checks (`scripts/rl_tasks/authored_checks.py`, `verify.mjs`, `structure_smoke.mjs`): they load `.nl`
    through the TS loader, which now accepts `protect:`; the Python checks read only `args` (authored_checks.py
    `_arg_counts`).
  - `improvement/program.ts` (`natlang improve CASE.json`): its own proposal search with adoption via `adopt`; adopt-call
    reuses the same `adoptSource`. WS8 N4 (`natlang improve DIR`) should call `adoptCall`'s gate rather than add a third.
- **Tests.** `ts-host/test/code-edits.test.mjs` (5 tests: protected/types/protect-list refusals with exact text,
  revision record, load error, adopt accept/reject/dry-run/stale, byte-identical rollback, refusal of failed and
  no-edit calls and of a forged protected revision, the CLI end to end with real `natlang check`). Conformance 22/22
  incl. 17-reopen-refine.

## 2026-11-23 Collector episodes judge refinements on their own driver (refined returns were undecidable)

- **Observation.** Authored probe `w900-refine` (helper `explain` returns `Is<string, "one sentence that says whose
  order the writer is talking about">`) failed qualification: reference replay and structure smoke both ended with
  `refinement-undecided: ... (no judge could decide it)`.
- **Cause.** `ts-host/src/teacher/collector.ts` `executeProgramInEpisode` builds `NodeNativeRuntime` with `agent:` and
  no `model` (collector.ts, the `new NodeNativeRuntime({ environment, agent: ... })` call), so `task.model()` is
  undefined, and `NatlangTask.refinementJudges` (`ts-host/src/runtime/runtime.ts`, `judgeOf`: `if (!config) return
  undefined;`) gave no judge. `RefinementChecker.check` then emits `source: 'none', outcome: 'undecided'`, and the
  kernel's post-call return check (`runtime/kernel.ts` `invokeDefinition`, `phase: 'return'`) fails the call. Same for
  refined arguments (kernel `phase: 'argument'`), `refine()` (`runtime/surface.ts`) and refined service results
  (`checkedServices`). Separately, the collector's one shared `NativeToolAgent` carried a refinement gate only with an
  item-result binding, and that gate had no judge either: no in-call repair, and refined root returns were never checked.
  So every refined function in RL collection, held eval and equivalence runs failed, not only the replay.
- **Fix (default, opt-out `NATLANG_COLLECTOR_REFINEMENT_JUDGE=0`).** New runtime option `agentDriver` (passed through
  `NodeNativeRuntime`): a task driven by `agent` with no model judges on that driver, by `decisionJudge` when it has
  `decide` (the policy's scorer: SGLang front / native engine `/v1/neuralese/decide`, sampled verdict in collection),
  else by `callJudge` (`holds` through the agent, which a reference child or a smoke child named `holds` answers). The
  collector passes its driver and builds the agent after the runtime, with the task's checker (shared verdict cache
  with the kernel check, so a sampled verdict is drawn once) and the task's judges (the `holds` call in the judged
  call's frame). Model-facing; recorded in `plans/MODEL_FACING_CHANGES.md`.
- **Inventory** (everything that runs programs through `executeProgram`): RL/EI collection and held eval
  (`run_bonsai_queue.py` -> `dist/teacher/collector.js` `collectBatch` -> `executeProgram`), `scripts/semantic_fp/
  equivalence.py` (held eval's execution), teacher generation (`teacher_gen.py` -> collector.js), reference replay
  (`curriculum.ts` `replayReference`/`referenceDriver`, `qualify_authored.py` verify), `structure_smoke.mjs`,
  `corrections.ts`, `handoff.ts`, `native-forced-replay.ts`, `improvement/teacher.ts`, ts-host scripts calling
  `executeProgram`: all covered by the one change. Not changed: evaluation fixtures (`teacher/evaluation-fixture.ts`
  `executeEvaluationFixture` -> `evaluate`, whose worker builds the runtime with `model: { driver }`,
  `evaluation/worker-entry.ts:58`, already judged); product runtimes with `model` (unchanged path); `interpreter({
  agent })` test fixtures without `agentDriver` (no judge, as before). Engines: no serving change; the judge uses the
  existing decide request every engine serves.
- **Result.** `ts-host/test/collector-refinement-judge.test.mjs` (5 tests: scorer true/false, scripted `holds`
  true/false, opt-out reproduces undecided). `qualify_authored.py` on `w900-refine` with the fixed runtime: PASS
  (reference admitted, smoke returns expected); with the opt-out: FAIL with the original `refinement-undecided`.

## 2026-11-23 Vibe Studio collection uses application functions and observed graphs

- **Decision.** Replace the universal `runUserGoal`/generic final-report collection contract across the entire Vibe Studio corpus with declared application entries, native typed inputs/results and a shared hierarchical Natlang library. User-requested outcomes and authorization remain checks; incidental child routes, discovery quotas and reread/order conventions do not. Runtime traces provide history. All 2,327 original goals/IDs/source groups/splits remain intact; all 116 entry signatures compile against the final library.
- **Mechanism.** Migrate the authored runner, service/outcome binders, Host collector/exporter, Python admission, independent JavaScript evidence verifier and native TypeScript materializer together. Preserve historical source identities. Add observed graph telemetry without an admission gate. Remove obsolete unregistered exporter checkers after checking actual registry bindings.
- **Acted-on defects.** Actual confined Eval CDP needed a kernel-issued socket capability and Workerd-specific inspector acknowledgements. A finite compiler witness had an incidental 30-second global watchdog; it now follows its actual enclosing lifecycle with an explicit timeout option. Completed model replies and running native values previously depended on final call persistence. Default incremental Core checkpoints, Base append-only model-exchange journals and Host ABI3 native emergency custody now acknowledge durable evidence, preserve original failed replies, and survive shared cleanup. Capture attachment epochs prevent teardown races; the resolved Luna identity is fenced before generation and scoring. The actual prepared-release startup also exposed stale generated producer catalogs for the new native archive RPC; regenerate the canonical catalogs, enforce freshness before every Host build/cache reuse and add exhaustive real attester/receiver parity coverage without weakening authorization.
- **Data.** Keep existing Sol and all raw failures. New teacher generation is Luna only. Additively recovered 14 trajectories/105 supported decisions comprise two completed goals/40 decisions and twelve partial trajectories/65 decisions. Partial decisions never complete a campaign goal. Native trajectory IR is the training representation; workspace replay/Program IR is not imposed. Registry publication is complete; ingestion, student reasoning fill and learner exposure remain separate recorded phases, respecting DGX's 15 GiB reserve and current SFT.
- **Evidence.** 116 production signatures, all-five clean Core vendors, 75 actual runtime/native SQLite integration tests, 276 Host kernel/real-inspector/lifecycle checks, 82 graph/export tests and a real Chromium OPFS interruption/reload smoke passed. Exact source pins, artifacts, remaining operational steps and limitations are in `VIBESTUDIO_SEMANTIC_CUTOVER_20261123.md`. Full collection uses shared infrastructure, eight workers, a 16 GiB cap and a 7.5 GiB Tick reserve; the fresh prepared release and live receipts determine the operational cutover, not a synthetic route qualification.
- **Archive throughput.** Actual retained state had 49,617 members/558 MB; the nearly full external HDD stalled checksum reads for minutes. Default lossless gzip-tar packing with member/SHA proofs reduces it to one 172 MB file (18.5 s, 594 MiB). Ordinary training artifacts stay directly readable; originals survive until verified transfer. Twenty-one focused tests and the quick gate passed. This is a Python-only producer change; no runtime/vendor repin.
- **Limits.** No new held success or learner exposure is claimed by this migration. The separately observed earlier connection reset is not retrospectively explained by the fixed CDP and watchdog defects. Preserve raw interruptions and diagnose new infrastructure failures rather than silently discarding data or indefinitely retrying a broken campaign.

## 2026-11-23 Higher-order semantic functions with checked signatures (semantic-FP B9, WS1 L4)

Shipped on main (default on; the model-facing note is off under `NATLANG_PROMPT_REVISION=2026-11-22`):
- **Uncalled `nl` where a function is expected** (`compiler/inline.ts`): an arrow argument whose parameter slot returns
  a function (`withRubric(rubric => nl`...`)`) takes that slot's signature; `nl-not-called` stays for slots that expect
  no function (`items.map(item => nl`...`)`). A factory without a declared result (`function judgeFor(rubric) { return
  nl`...`; }`, or an arrow) takes its parameters from how the functions it makes are called (`judgeFor(r)(t)`, `const
  j = judgeFor(r); j(t)`); before, it silently planned `() => unknown`. Return position and function-typed fields with
  declared types already worked (checked, now tested).
- **Function types are checked signatures.** `targets.ts` converts an asynchronous TS function type (or a
  `NatlangFunction`) to the natlang function type `(t: T) => R` (before: a `Live<..., "function">` host value, and an
  inline nl parameter of `NatlangFunction` type was refused as an intersection). The grammar reads `=> Promise<R>` as
  `=> R`. Every natlang callable carries `NATLANG_SIGNATURE` (lazy, from its definition); `coerce` checks it with
  `signatureFits` (positional parameters, contravariant; covariant result; the definer's aliases compared by
  definition) and refuses with `function-signature-mismatch`. `fitsType` on lambdas is now positional (parameter names
  had to match before). A plain TS function at a function-typed slot is wrapped (one wrapper per function and slot type)
  so each call checks its arguments and awaited result; an eval's own annotated locals keep their functions unwrapped
  (`functions: 'keep'`). Eval and `.d.nl.ts` TypeScript render natlang function types with a promised result.
- **`fn.partial(...leading)`** binds the first parameters, as `bind` does (positional, so TypeScript types it exactly:
  `partial<B extends Partial<A>>(...bound: B): NatlangFunction<NatlangDropBound<A, B>, R>`), checks them at once, and
  keeps `on`, `in` (via `inContext`: the rebound original, partially applied), `with` and `iterateOn`. Decision: positional
  rather than by name, because tuple labels are not visible to TypeScript types and JS's `bind` is positional.
  `partial` is a reserved callable property.
- **Call note** for a call whose result is a function: build it in eval and finish with it (`native/prompt.ts`
  `functionResultNote`, through `callNotes` for the runtime and the training rebuild). MODEL_FACING_CHANGES entry.
- **Docs/example:** new `examples/screening` (`meets.partial(requirement)` checks plus `fit_for.nl`, whose result is a
  function), built and run in `authoring-examples.test.mjs`; composition.md "Functions that take and return judgments",
  language.md types bullets, SPEC Types, ERRORS + skill error table rows.

Gaps from B3/B4, fixed here:
- `Record<Verdict, number>` (alias key): the dictionary carries its key alias and `TypeEnv.resolve` makes it the exact
  record when the alias resolves to string literals (B3 had made it a plain dictionary); `Record<K, number>` with
  `K = number` names the problem.
- `Folder.propose`/`apply` inferred `R = unknown` for a reducer whose parameter was annotated: TypeScript's subtype pass
  of overload resolution fails `any` against the annotation and picks the `unknown` fallback overload. The reducer's
  folder parameter is now typed `FolderHandle` (what the runtime passes). `examples/refunds/ledger.ts` drops
  `propose<[], Ledger>`.
- Target arguments: `Request[]` with a program `Request` (containing `Untrusted`) was refused as the built-in host
  `Request` before `types.ts` was read. The parse-time check skips shadowable built-in names; the full check follows the
  program's aliases in `describeArguments`/`readTargetArguments`. The message now says what cannot be written.
- Unreadable `types.ts` aliases: `parseAliases` turns an alias the grammar cannot read into a marker that reports
  `type X is not in the natlang type grammar (...)` only where a signature uses it. Used by every eager builder:
  `loader.ts` (checkSignature, decision domain), `values.ts` buildPending, `kernel.ts` refinedSignature (which silently
  dropped refinement checks for the whole call when any alias failed), `refined-slots.ts` (same silent loss),
  `lowered.ts`, `nz-file.ts`, `target-arguments.ts` (mapped unreadable aliases to `unknown`), `app/playground.ts`,
  `callable.ts`. Left out: `compiler/idiom.ts:57` (B11's uncommitted file; same one-line change applies).

Inventory and what is not applicable: engines receive only rendered prompt text and the tool schema; `schemaOf`
(`native/agent.ts:280-297`) emits `{}` for function types as before, so no engine (llama-server, wllama, Python native,
SGLang) changes. Python renderers replay recorded system messages; `serving-request.ts` composes the new note via
`callNotes`. Browser: same sources through `platformDefaults` (`browser/index.ts:52`), tested in higher-order.test.mjs.

## 2026-11-23 Structural recursion in `.nl` and `ensures:` postconditions (semantic-FP B12, WS1 L7)

Shipped on main (opt-in per function by frontmatter; the prompt sentence fix is the default, off under
`NATLANG_PROMPT_REVISION=2026-11-22`):
- **Recursion.** `recursive: structural` or `measure: "<TS over the arguments>"` in a `.nl` frontmatter. The kernel
  (`runtime/kernel.ts` `runDefinitionBody`) keeps a chain of active recursive `.nl` calls (`Frame.nlActive`) and admits
  a re-entry when the arguments descend by the same guard TypeScript functions use (`runtime/context.ts` `descend`,
  now exported) or the measure (a non-negative whole number, evaluated in a synthetic callable-folder module) falls.
  Undeclared re-entry, a non-descending argument and a non-falling measure are `NatlangRecursionError`s with one
  sentence each. The function is bound under its own name in its calls' scope (`definitionNode` adds `self`).
  Decision: the descent guard also counts an equal copy of a proper part of plain acyclic data as a part, for
  TypeScript too, because an `.nl` call receives its arguments as realm copies (identity never matched); size strictly
  falls along such a chain, so termination holds. `MAX_AD_HOC_NL_DEPTH` stays 5; no size heuristic (v1's) was built.
- **`ensures:`** (`runtime/ensures.ts` parse/validate, `runtime/contracts.ts` run): `check:` clauses (TS over `result`,
  arguments, companion items, standard globals) run first on read-only copies, compiled through the normal module
  lowering; `predicate:` clauses with `against:` are judged by the refinement checker with the named arguments as
  context (the judge message gains a context block, untrusted text fenced at any depth; the verdict key includes the
  context; crisp checkers skip relational obligations). Failures are `refinement-unsatisfied`/`-undecided` at `return`:
  the agent's return gate and staged-result check ask `lam.ensures` after the refined slots, so they re-enter the
  refinement repair budget; the kernel checks again after any path (memoized per result). Items a `check:` names are
  protected via `loader.ts` `recordProtectedSources` (inside `treeProtectedSources`, B8's one place) and
  `definitionNode`; `edit_code` refuses edits that change `ensures:`/`measure:`/`recursive:`. `refine(value, p,
  { context })` uses the same path (lowering passes options after the type-argument predicate). `natlang check` lists
  `ensures` clauses with the refined slots. Load errors: shape, parse, unknown name, `against` not an argument, an
  argument named `result`.
- **Fixed on the way:** SPEC's frontmatter-keys sentence was duplicated (B8 merge); `signatureFits` (B9) treated an
  alias the slot's scope does not define as foreign and refused `(text) => Draft` against itself (interpreter test
  "a type alias from an earlier eval ..." was red at fb20452d1); `loadNamedFunction` checked names before attaching
  `uses:`. Test hygiene: verdicts persist in the machine call store, so tests that count judge passes open their own
  `CallStore`.
- **Docs/example:** `examples/outline` (recursive `digest.nl` with a check helper and a judged predicate), built and run
  in `authoring-examples.test.mjs` and quoted in composition.md; SPEC (Postconditions; Iteration and termination),
  ERRORS, refinements ext, authoring skill (language, refinements, verification, SKILL error table), integration
  refinements recovery table. Tests: `nl-recursion.test.mjs`, `relational-refinements.test.mjs`.

Inventory: engines receive only prompt text (the system sentence; the judge's user message when context is present)
through the existing scoring and tool protocol, so llama-server, wllama, Python native and SGLang need no change
(`decisionJudge`, `native/refinement.ts`, is the one client that builds the judge request). Python renderers replay
recorded system messages (`pieces.json` regenerated with history). Training consumers (`scripts/rl_tasks/*`) load `.nl`
through the TS loader, so the new keys parse there. Browser: same sources; the contract module uses
`moduleInstanceAsync` where the realm is async. Not done: a `readout: decision` result that breaks `ensures:` fails the
call (no re-pick of the next option); `natlang check` checks the names in `check:`/`measure:` expressions, not their
types.

## 2026-11-23 B16: `natlang:learning` conformance runs end to end on the Python native engine (semantic-FP WS8 N1)

- **Cases.** All 10 pending cases of `conformance/neuralese/cases/termination-learning-graph.yaml` are `implemented`
  and green: `grad-context-item`, `grad-stop-gradient`, `grad-nested-first-order`, `grad-log-likelihood`,
  `graph-replay-fixed-choices`, the four `iterate-*` cases and `learning-requires-service`. Runnable forms:
  `ts-host/test/conformance/learning.mjs`.
- **Runner.** `ts-host/scripts/native-conformance.mjs` (check-main's `ts-conformance` step, full check only) now also
  reads the behavioural cases. It checks that every `implemented_by` exists and runs the conformance-module forms
  itself. Cases with `engines: [python-native]` run against `tests/neuralese/learning_conformance_server.py`, a real
  Python native engine on the tiny LFM backbone of the native harness tests. Every forward, native write and import,
  recorded turn, replay and gradient there is the engine's own. Only token selection is a fixture policy (`default`
  and `alt`, switchable over stdin), and so is the driver's typed readout. The engine runs on CUDA when present.
  All ten cases take about 50 s.
- **How the replay checks hold.** The case records under the `default` policy and replays under `alt`, where every
  choice differs. It then requires an equal loss and gradient, zero generation requests during the replay and one
  effect call per recording. "Model weights unchanged" is a SHA-256 of the live parameters, taken before and after.
- **Bugs found and fixed (each was a real failure of a case):**
  1. A soft value written by an earlier task, such as a context item, carries its writer's `source_occurrence`.
     `NativeToolAgent.modelTurnNode` refused to read it ("names no matching in-episode writer"), while `blockInput`
     (graph.ts) binds such a read as `external`, as NEURALESE_GRAPH "Record" says. The agent now agrees with it. A
     recorded request (one under a learning recorder) also drops occurrences its trajectory does not hold
     (`localNativeOccurrences`, applied in the Neuralese server transport), so the request, the server's capture and
     the graph events agree on the external read.
  2. An arrow-function model driver gave the actor id `''` (`kernel.ts` used `??` on `driver.name`), and every recorded
     native turn then failed with `invalid actor`. It is now `model`, as in the agent.
  3. First-order nesting was wrong: an inner `grad` plus an optimizer step inside an order-1 `grad` gave the root no
     gradient, because the updated state was unrelated to it. The derivative program now takes `order: 1`, where the
     inner gradient nodes are detached (constants). An order-1 gradient whose loss updates its argument runs through it,
     so the outer gradient passes the update with its Jacobian at constant g. With plain SGD that equals ∇L at s', and
     the case checks this.
  4. The derivative program never reached its roots through an update, at either order. The recorded turns after a host
     optimizer step import the host's own updated artifact. The program recomputes that update under a different ID
     (its provenance differs), so the outer replay read the recorded artifact as a constant. The `order: 2` gradient
     through native-state updates was exactly zero. Optimizer nodes now carry `recorded` (the host's artifact ID), and
     `_rewrite_request` maps it to the recomputed value. Contract changes are on both sides
     (`native_derivative_contract.py`, `native-derivative-contract.ts`). The existing order-2 adapter fixture
     (`native-adapter-recorded-learning.mjs`) checked only provenance, which is why this went unseen. Adapters take the
     same path; their nonzero order-2 gradient is not asserted anywhere yet.
- **Engines.** `docs/ENGINE_PARITY.md` has a gradients row with each engine's blocker: llama.cpp and wllama have no
  backward pass, and the SGLang actor has no gradient replay endpoint. Training runs on the Python native engine and
  hands states and adapters to the others as files.
- **Not checked.** The non-layer state tensors (`embeddings`, `token_ids`, `positions`) get no gradient; the case
  asserts that this is the server's root inventory and does not check whether `embeddings` should be a root. Nothing
  was measured on LFM3 weights; the tiny backbone checks mechanism, not learning quality. An order-2 gradient inside
  an order-1 gradient whose loss updates its argument is refused (`learning-grad-order`). `ERRORS.md` gained
  `learning-unavailable`, which existed in code but had no row.

## 2026-11-23 07:00 `@natlang/std` skeleton: convergence and workspace combinators with shipped `.nl` judgments (semantic-FP B13, WS3 S2)

**Shipped.** `@natlang/node/std` / `@natlang/browser/std` (also `std` from `@natlang/node`): `semanticRepair`,
`fixedPoint`, `semanticMerge`, `proposeAndVerify`, `branchAndSelect` (`ts-host/src/std/`). Their own judgments are
`.nl` files in `ts-host/std/` (`intentOf`, `compatible`, `combine`, `settled`, `beats`; the three finite ones are
`readout: decision`), embedded byte for byte by `scripts/generate-builtin.mjs` (`src/std/sources.generated.ts`),
loaded as ordinary named functions under `@natlang/std/<name>.nl` and exported so programs can `decide`, `.in`, `.on`
and replace them. Decomposition: `ts-host/std/DECOMPOSITION.md`. Every run records a `std:<name>` trace with one
`std_stage` event per stage naming that stage's call IDs (nested combinators appear by reference).

**Decisions.**
- Bounds: `semanticRepair` needs `attempts` and `fixedPoint` with an exact `settled` needs `maxSteps`, the same rule
  `iterateOn` has for TypeScript predicates (`iteration-unbounded`). `fixedPoint`'s default stop is the shipped
  `settled` judgment, which needs no bound (progress judge). At the bound both return their closest value
  (`ok`/`settled: false`) instead of throwing: a deliberate answer.
- `proposeAndVerify` is `semanticRepair` over proposals (one repair loop); each retry starts from the failed draft
  (`draft.select(previous.folder)` inside an `APPLY_TO_FOLDER` reducer, so there is no nested transaction).
- `semanticMerge` keeps `base` at unresolved paths by default (only vetted edits enter); combined values must be the

## 2026-11-22 23:30 GRPO decision-only steps: the step's data factor counts units and scales the gradient; KL telemetry per value (decision hunt)

Observations (LoRA bench, 7c9038cf5, grpo-v4/run2 replay, 6 groups/step): steps 1 and 6 trained only sampled decisions
(16 and 24, 3-option `</think>"pass|fail|needs-review"<|im_end|>` readouts) with pre-clip grad_norm 65 and 23 against
0.2-0.3 on chain steps; step 1 KL 0, step 6 kl_mean 860.

- **Cause.** Under `--loss-norm token` a step's loss is the mean over its own units, and a decision in an episode with no
  token call is 1 unit, so each decision weighed 1/16-1/24 (1/~10,000 in a mixed step). The 16 decisions were 2
  distinct choices (sibling episodes repeat a decision), so their gradients add coherently: that is the norm ratio.
  `lr_data_scale` counted the 2 decision groups like chain groups (2/12), so one AdamW step (a sign step at step 1:
  LoRA B = 0) at LR 8.3e-6 went to two choices. It moved an unseen prompt of the same family by up to 3.2 nats
  (`needs-review` up, the direction the advantages select: summed by option over steps 1-5, needs-review +8.4,
  fail -7.8) and the behaviour probe's end-of-turn logp by +1.35. AdamW's moments (beta2 0.99) then carried that
  clipped gradient (norm 1 against 0.2-0.3) into steps 2-5 at their LR while decisions were 1e-4 of those steps'
  gradient; by step 6 option-softmax d reached 7.5 nats. kl_mean 860 = k3 (e^d) of that d, summed over the 24
  softmax values plus ~146 chosen-token values and divided by 24 units.
- **Fixes (1601076d9, defaults with opt-outs, tests in test_grpo_learner.py):**
  - `spread_data`: each group with spread counts min(1, its loss units / `--lr-reference-group-units` 4096) in
    `lr_data_scale` (0: one per group). A decision group of 8 is ~0.002 of a group; production groups (~100k units)
    and the bench's chain groups count ~1.
  - `scale_and_clip`: the same factor scales the gradient before the clip, so the moments carry a small step at its
    size (`--no-data-scaled-gradient` opts out). `grad_norm` stays the mean-loss norm; `grad_norm_applied` is logged.
  - KL telemetry divides by its values (`kl_n`), not the loss units; `decision_kl_k2_mean` (option softmax) and
    `decision_token_kl_k2_mean` (chosen-option tokens) are logged apart.
  - Identical sampled decisions share one forward (`decision_forward_key`); each keeps its term.
- **Re-run** (`ops/grpo-v6/bench-lora-20261122/dechunt/`, main fb20452d1 vs the same code with
  `--lr-reference-group-units 0 --no-data-scaled-gradient`; schedule = the bench's step-1 then step-6 batches):
  old: step 1 lr 8.3e-6, applied grad 64.4, end_logp_change +1.35, step-6 batch option scores vs the reference up
  to +3.19, kl_mean 0.90 (decision k2 1.62). New: step 1 lr 1.6e-8, applied grad 0.021, end_logp_change +0.015,
  option scores within 0.54 (centered within ~0.2; the rest is a common shift on the shared tail tokens), kl_mean 0.009.
  Decision forward+backward 5-10 s (32.8 s at step 1 of the original bench, before dedup). CUDA peak 12.2 GiB.
- **Ruled out / checked:** clip (rescales only; step 1 is a sign step either way); reference view (step-1 KL exactly 0,
  reference scores of a prompt identical at steps 2 and 6); warmup (0.5x at step 1, as designed); decision tensors
  (positions/targets/owner; learner = reference at step 1); rows untied (`load_base_model` refuses an untied head);
  the step-1 learner/actor gap (|log rho| 0.6 at "stale 0"): the replayed groups were sampled by run2's versions 2-12
  (`served_policy`), the replay labels them fresh; the record's `policy` field is the start checkpoint id.
  Independent static review (second investigator) agreed on normalization, data scale and AdamW; it raised the gap
  above, which the served versions explain.
- **Open findings (not fixed here):**
  - SGLang decision scores are nondeterministic: identical (served version, prompt, options) rows differ by median

## 2026-11-23 decision parity: FP8 KV, BF16 head logits, options' shared tokens

Hunt on the semantic-FP B10 decision-parity run (`ops/semantic-fp/decision-parity/`, sft-v8 66422fcf; the Colab A100
front d3ad57fb). Measurements on a diagnostic SGLang beside the A100 actor (same export, vendor projection, 8 GB) and
the native engine on the A100 and GB10 (scripts in the session scratchpad; per-token data under
`ops/semantic-fp/decision-parity/hunt-20261123/`).

- **Observation 1 (score vs sentinel on one server, up to 0.49 nats; native vs SGLang up to 3.74, TV 0.27).** Cause:
  SGLang input log-probs depend on what a request is batched with and where a radix hit splits its prefill, and the
  actor's unscaled FP8 e4m3 KV amplifies that ~3x. Same server, same ids: sequential repeats are bitwise identical;
  radix reuse alone (prompt > 256 tokens) moves an option by <= 0.2; concurrent requests by up to 1.66 (FP8) / 0.51
  (BF16 KV); the front's schedule (items on 16 threads, the first option then the rest in parallel) by 0.74-0.80 (FP8)
  / 0.26 (BF16). `--enable-deterministic-inference` makes every schedule bitwise equal (0.000) but disables the radix
  cache with FlashInfer, so it is no actor default. Native vs SGLang: FP8 KV TV mean 0.038 / max 0.27 / argmax 43 of
  44 (reproduces the run); BF16 KV TV 0.012 / 0.051 / 44 of 44, per-token |d| mean 0.042 -> 0.011, max 3.7 -> 0.26.
  K/V e4m3 rounding error is 2.65% RMS per element in every attention layer, the same with a per-layer amax scale
  (mantissa, not range: no free fix by calibrated scales).
- **Fixed (defaults, opt-outs, tests):**
  - Head logits leave the head GEMM in FP32 on every Python path and SGLang: BF16 logits near |20| step by 0.125, and
    the native engine's own full-forward vs token-stepped scores of one sequence differed by mean 0.066 / max 0.41
    nats (FP32: 0.034 / 0.18). Learner `lfm3_fast._head_logits_chunk` (gradients still rounded to BF16, chunk halved
    to keep its bytes), native `shared_state.logits` / `fused_moe.invariant_linear(output_dtype=)` (batch invariant,
    straight-through under autograd so training reads the same logits), SGLang `--enable-fp32-lm-head`
    (`serve_native_checkpoint --sglang-head-logits fp32`, attested as `serving_engine.head_logits`, a held pairing
    field). Opt-outs `NATLANG_HEAD_LOGITS=bf16`, `--sglang-head-logits bf16`. llama.cpp computes F32 logits already.
  - Tokens every option shares are prompt, not choice (`native_learning._shared_into_prompt`; sft_sources decision
    rows carry them as `prefix`, `exp0_sft.decision_parts` reads them as prompt; decision captures, tune rows and
    native graph rows follow `decision_items`; fork commit on llama.cpp-neuralese, below). Opt-out
    `NATLANG_DECISION_SHARED_PREFIX=option`. On the FP8 actor this lowers the front-vs-sequential option-score gap
    (median 0.139 -> 0.112, max 0.74 -> 0.53); the normalized readout gap stays (TV mean 0.020 -> 0.018): the rest is
    the options' own tokens under batch-variant FP8 arithmetic.
  - Managed llama-server: the release's `chat_template_kwargs` (LFM3 `preserve_thinking`) are server defaults
    (`--chat-template-kwargs`): `/v1/natlang/score` renders items with the defaults only, and a readout's opening
    assistant turn lost its reasoning there (`<think></think>`), unlike generation and the Python engines.
- **Deliberately not changed: FP8 KV stays the collection/held default.** At collection concurrency the KV reads
  dominate decode on the GB10 (aei1: 145 running, ~1.1-1.3M tokens resident, ~7 GB FP8 KV per decode step against ~2 GB
  of FP8 weights); BF16 KV would roughly double them and needs ~2x `--sglang-kv-gb`. The learner corrects the actor
  law with importance weights; held pairs within one KV dtype. `--sglang-kv-cache-dtype auto` is the opt-in where
  fidelity matters more than throughput (decision-parity checks, scoring-heavy servers).
- **Observation 2 (-17 to -24 nats per option).** `</think>` right after the generation prompt's `<think>` costs
  16.4 nats (14.5-18.2) and was scored in every option; the rest averages -4.9. It is never a training target (own
  readout rows weight it 0, 87% of own rows train reasoning at that position) and every consumer (softmax readout,
  field-mode product, temperature sampling, `decision_loss`) is shift invariant, so it never moved a probability or a
  floor; it only added per-option noise on SGLang (fixed above). Sampling the model on the 10 joint prompts (16 each,
  T=1, top-p 0.95, BF16 KV): it reasons ~400 tokens and its answers differ from the no-think readout: same mode on 7
  of 10, mean TV 0.31 (answerInvite: readout `accept` p=0.40, sampled `decline` 16/16, which the calendar supports).
  The readout is a separate no-reasoning policy (trained by readout rows and the decision objective), not the
  generation policy; its confidence is that policy's. Whether `decide` should read options after a sampled reasoning
  is a product decision for the readout's owner (cost ~400 generated tokens per decision).
- **Open:** the in-page engine scores with its template defaults too (`preserve_thinking` false: the vendored wllama
  applies `default_template_kwargs` only to chat completions) and the fork's shared-prefix commit; both enter with the
  next fork release (ENGINE_PARITY). Not checked: CUDA graphs (decode only; scoring prefills run eager), overlap

## 2026-11-23 reasoned decisions: `readout: decision` reasons first, then scores; `readout: instant` is the fast mode

**Decision (coordinator, from the 2026-11-23 decision-score hunt; this entry records it).** A decision readout samples
the model's own reasoning on the readout request, then scores its options conditioned on that reasoning. That is the
default of `readout: decision`, `decisionReadout: 'finite-returns'` and the std judgments. The no-reasoning readout
stays as `readout: instant` (a new value of the existing `readout:` key: no new frontmatter key, one new word). Trace
specialization and the compile ladder recover cost on hot paths. Why: the instant readout described a weaker
no-reasoning policy (argmax = the model's reasoned answer on 7 of 10 prompts, mean TV 0.31; answerInvite `accept`
p 0.40 vs `decline` 16/16), and floors and escalation read its confidence.

- **Semantics.** `decisionSamples` reasoning samples per readout (default 4, `NATLANG_DECISION_SAMPLES`, model config;
  1 at temperature 0; 0 = instant everywhere), drawn in parallel at the call's temperature on the unchanged readout
  messages. Each option is scored as the content after the sample's reasoning (`<think>R</think>option`). A value's
  probability is the mean over samples of its softmax after that reasoning: a Monte Carlo estimate of the reasoned
  policy's answer distribution (the model's chance of answering with it when it reasons first). Scores are the model's
  own log-probabilities, never tempered; temperature only shapes the reasoning drawn. Answer = mixture argmax; under an
  RL sampling scorer, one seeded sample is the action and its sampled choice is the answer (a draw from the mixture).
  Several samples rather than one: after its reasoning the model is almost always certain (the scored option equals
  the answer it then wrote in 155/155 samples), so one sample's conditional is ~0/1 and a floor would read noise.
- **Engines (one wire field, score item `reasoning`).** Python native and SGLang: `native_learning.decision_items(...,
  reasoning=)` (shared-prefix rule puts R and `</think>` in the prompt; results echo `reasoning: true`, captures record
  it). llama.cpp fork 0bee37915 on `neuralese` (token ids equal to Python on 3 items incl. `open_reply`); release run
  45120615947 queued behind run 45117905605; the runtime pin moves with the next `update_llama_runtime --fork`. Until
  then the managed server and the page do not echo: the client refuses (`decision-reasoning-unsupported`), traces it and
  reads out instantly for that driver (ENGINE_PARITY gap row). Client: `decision-scoring.ts` (batch item + echo check;
  prompt_logprobs route puts the reasoning on the assistant message), `neuralese-server.ts`, browser `local-model.ts`.
- **Captures and training.** Reasoning turns: phase `decision_reasoning` in trajectories, `decision_reasoning` on
  recorded turns, no execution-graph node; decision entries carry `assistant.reasoning` and `decision_reasoning:
  {index, samples, action}`; the collector samples only the action. SFT (B5 objective): in a verified success each sample
  whose answer equals the action's trains the option CE conditioned on its own reasoning plus the reasoning tokens as
  own targets (`decision_graph.reasoned_decision_plan`, `exp0_sft` reasoning NLL; opt-out `--no-decision-reasoning`);
  other samples and groups without an action are not trained. `sft_sources.ReplayEpisode` answers a reasoned group from
  its action entry as one call. GRPO: the choice is conditioned on R (capture prompt ids); R's tokens are not trained
  there (open). Tune rollouts push the action sample only.
- **Calibration (same 10 prompts, sft-v8, native engine, the hunt's 16 recorded reasoned samples each;
  `ops/semantic-fp/decision-parity/reasoned-20261123/reasoned.json`).** Readout vs the reasoned answers of the 12
  held-out samples: instant TV 0.30, mode 8/10 -> reasoned (k=4) TV 0.12, mode 9/10. Vs all 16: 0.31 / 7 -> 0.09 / 10.
  answerInvite: instant `accept` 0.38 -> reasoned `decline` 1.00; routeEmail 0.50 -> 1.00; moderatePost and rateBug move
  to the sampled mode. Mean of all 16 conditionals vs the 16 answers: TV 0.000.
- **B13 `compatible.nl` cases (sft-v6, the current policy, native server; `compatible-v2.json`).** Four reconstructed cases (the B13 diag
  program is gone; texts from `examples/release` and B13's entry): P(compatible) instant -> reasoned (k=16), and the
  answers the 16 reasoning turns wrote: additive highlights, clean intents (gold true) 0.057 -> 0.189 (2 true / 12
  false / 2 cut off at 4096 tokens); same with the model's intents (true) 0.128 -> 0.120 (1/14/1); version clash
  (false) 0.023 -> 0.000 (0/16); release titles (false) 0.057 -> 0.000 (0/16). **Reasoning does not fix it:** the
  readout now ranks the compatible cases above the clashes (it did not before) and its numbers match what the model
  answers when it reasons, but the reasoned policy itself judges additive edits incompatible (14 of 16 answers), so
  every merge is still judged incompatible at any sensible floor. It stays a training target (WS5
  `semantic-convergence`, as B13 recorded); the reasoned readout makes the floor read the policy's actual belief. The
  compatible cases also reason long (two samples hit 4096 tokens): `compatible` is a candidate for `readout: instant`
  or a specialized path once trained.
- **Also fixed:** `nl` called on literal instructions (``nl(`...`(x))``, ``nl(`...`, x)``, ``nl(`...`)(x)``) compiles as
  the tag form on every compile path (compiler host, eval, host cells) with identical plans and identity; `nl-not-tag`
  stays for run-time-built text (now one sentence naming that cause) and `nl` as a value (B13's live loop;
  MODEL_FACING_CHANGES); a reasoning reply
  cut off before `</think>` is still used as the reasoning; `model-call-kinds.json` declares `decision-reasoning` and the
  `/v1/neuralese/sentinel` route; a guessed (`discover`) score endpoint answering non-score JSON counts as absent.
- **Open.** The Python engines strip the reasoning text (`chat.build_message` `.strip()`), so the scored prompt can differ
  from the sampled ids at the edges (`build.json` `decision_reasoning_ids_exact` counts it; the rendered ids train).
  Stock-model frames (`decision-frame.ts`) score a framed request after reasoning sampled on the unframed one. Not run:
  SGLang end to end with reasoning, the page, a full collection with reasoned readouts, held eval.

## 2026-11-23 08:20 Verifier tasks over the @natlang/std combinators (sfp3): std now runs in collection, 9 batches, 73 train rows in grpo-pool

The coordinator asked for this batch because live LFM3 scored additive edits as less compatible than real clashes in
`compatible.nl` (B13). The tasks are programs that use `semanticMerge`, `semanticRepair`, `fixedPoint`,
`proposeAndVerify` and `branchAndSelect` with the shipped judgments (no overrides), and their verifiers judge the outcome.

  - *First bug.* The collector loads the runtime without the package entry, so `@natlang/node/std` in callable-folder
    TypeScript fell through to the package loader. That ran a second copy of the runtime, which has no active task
    ("No natlang task is active here"). Now `platform-defaults.ts` registers the standard library on every platform.
  - *Second bug.* `semanticMerge` treated records built in the module realm as opaque values, because they have
    another `Object.prototype`, so the whole record became one conflict. A single realm-tolerant `isPlainObject`
    (`runtime/plain-object.ts`) now serves std and seven other places that tested `=== Object.prototype`: native
    values and runtime, canonical data, call normalization, folder iteration, folder Python, the learning module and the
    teacher materializer.
  - The async module path also exports `Context`. Test: `ts-host/test/std-platform-entry.test.mjs` imports only the Node
    platform.
- **Merge verifier.** New verifier `merge.mjs` (fe8efaa41). It checks that a judged field equals an accepted value or
  contains each compatible edit's piece. It also checks that `unresolved` lists exactly the incompatible paths. Where a
  reading is genuinely two-way, `{any: [...]}` and `unresolved_optional` accept both.
- **Construct tags.** New tags `semantic_merge`, `semantic_repair`, `fixed_point`, `propose_and_verify` and
  `branch_and_select`, each checked statically (the program imports the combinator and calls it). The repetition

## 2026-11-23 13:45 Memory ledger: conservative backfill (no head-of-line starvation, no blocked small jobs)

- **Observation:** on 2026-11-23 a 32 GB medium held measurement (`heldv4-measure-v2-sft-v6`) sat at the queue head
  for 4 h behind aei1's 74 GB collection; the 1 GB `natlang-storage-sweep-run` (class service, `--no-resumable`)
  failed 12 times in 12 h on its 1500 s wait while disk fell below its floor (at 12:53 it was refused with 7.9 GiB free
  for a 1+1 GiB need); 1.5 GB `--no-resumable` drain units waited over an hour.
- **Cause (two halves of one rule):** backfill behind a blocked head was allowed for any *resumable* job and for no
  other. (1) Non-resumable jobs and services, however small, could never backfill. (2) Resumable jobs of the head's own
  priority backfilled without limit, and the head cannot preempt them (preemption takes strictly lower priority only),
  so the stream of 2-17 GB medium jobs took each GB the head was waiting for: a 4 h starvation, not FIFO.
- **Rule (`memory_ledger.may_backfill`, default on):** a job behind the head may start when it fits by real headroom
  and cannot delay the head: `spare` (its start still leaves the head's whole budget + reserve free), or, while the head
  is blocked even with preemption (`head_blocked`), `reclaimable` (resumable and strictly lower priority: the head
  takes the room back by preemption, as before) or `lent` (its budget fits within a quarter of the head's remaining
  shortfall, i.e. its need minus everything it could obtain by preemption as if nothing had been lent, minus the
  budgets already lent behind it). Without per-job runtimes (the ledger has none) a size cap is the sound simple form
  of conservative backfill: the shortfall falls only as the units the head waits on end, so lending shrinks to zero as
  the head nears its start, finished backfills never re-open the allowance, and the head's extra wait is bounded by at
  most a quarter of its original shortfall having to free on top (a simulated never-ending stream of same-priority
  2 GiB jobs delays a 40 GiB head by <= 4 polls; the old rule never admitted it). Priorities and preemption semantics
  are unchanged; a high head is protected by the same cap.
- **Opt-out:** `NATLANG_LEDGER_BACKFILL=legacy` (in the environment of `run` and of the guard) restores the old rule.
- **Visibility:** claims record `backfilled_behind` and `backfill` (`spare|reclaimable|lent`, `legacy` for older
  claims); `status` lists `backfilled`, `backfill_mode`, and for a blocked head `lent_gb` and
  `backfill_allowance_gb`; `admitted`/`relaunched` events carry both fields.
- **Live pickup:** new `run` calls of `/home/werg/natlang/scripts/memory_ledger.py` use it at once; the guard (requeued
  relaunches) was restarted; `run` waiters launched from pinned or archived copies of the script keep the old rule
  until they end. Tests: `tests/test_memory_ledger.py` (lent/large/spare/reclaimable fixtures, guard relaunch within
  the allowance, run + status, starvation simulation under both modes).
- **Storage sweep:** `natlang-storage-sweep-run` is now `--resumable` (it is a rerunnable deletion pass): as a low
  job behind a medium/high head it backfills as `reclaimable` whenever 1+1 GiB fits, instead of only within a lent
  allowance (at 13:29 the allowance was used up by legacy same-priority backfills behind `aei1-r0001-build`). Unit file
  updated in `scripts/systemd/` and `~/.config/systemd/user/`; admitted at 13:30 as `reclaimable`.

## 2026-11-23 16:00 Expert-iteration ledger priorities: round stages outrank collections (priority inversion fix)

- **Observation.** The standing aei1 DGX collection (`ensure_collection`, ledger priority high, ~74 GB) held its own
  round's build (`aei1-r0001-build`, 24 GB, medium) for 96 minutes. The ledger preempts only resumable units of
  strictly lower priority, so a medium stage could never take memory from a high collection, and every medium job
  queued behind the blocked build. The supervisor stopped the collection by hand.
- **Decision.** Fix it in the ledger's own terms rather than with driver-side yielding: `STAGE_PRIORITY = 'high'` for
  every critical-path stage (async `frontier`, `data`, `build`, DGX SFT, GRPO, `publish`; the cycle's `frontier`,
  `data`, `build`; launch-sft.sh is already high) and `COLLECTION_PRIORITY = 'medium'` (resumable, the ledger default)
  for every collection (the standing DGX one, remote collection clients, a cycle's collect and recollect; opt-out:
  `NATLANG_EI_COLLECTION_PRIORITY=high` in the driver's environment). A waiting
  stage now preempts the collection; the ledger requeues it with its launch spec (same policy, pin and work dir), the
  collector resumes from its scored groups (`collect`: first group after the last, `already_scored`), and the fill
  waits for the actor on the same port (`filled_reasoning` retries a refused actor for 4 h). This also covers the
  cross-process case a driver-side yield cannot (another driver's collection blocking a cycle's build), and other
  agents' medium smokes and evals still cannot preempt the collection (equal priority). Driver-side stopping was
  rejected: the cycle path's collection belongs to another process whose collect stage exits on a stopped collection,
  and restart bookkeeping races the DGX SFT's own stop.
- **Requeue-awareness.** `Cycle.present(unit)` = active or `ledger_queued`; `Cycle.ledger` joins a requeued unit
  instead of launching it twice, `Cycle.wait` and the cycle's collect loop wait through a requeue, and
  `ensure_collection`, `ensure_remote_collection`, `stop_collections` (so a DGX SFT cancels a requeued collection
  instead of the ledger relaunching it beside the learner), `prepare`'s snapshot wait and the halt/recollect paths use
  it. Side effect: a collection no longer outranks a DGX held measurement (both medium); held keeps its slot share.
- **Open.** A preempted cycle collection gets a fresh `--hours` window from its relaunch (`collect` sets the deadline
  at start); harmless for the standing async collection (long horizon), it can lengthen a cycle's collect stage.
- **Rollout.** aei1 untouched; the coordinator moves it onto the new pin at the next round boundary. Tests:
  `test_round_stages_preempt_the_standing_collection_which_resumes_on_its_policy` (test_async_train.py, including
  `memory_ledger.preemption_plan` with the real priorities) and
  `test_cycle_stages_outrank_its_collection_and_a_requeued_unit_is_joined` (test_expert_iteration.py).

## 2026-11-23 instant readout collapse (B14 C-instant 4/28): the readout scored a reply form the checkpoint does not answer in

**Observations (B14, b0fe8d310).** `examples/triage` at 19844f4d on the `bench-base` native profile (checkpoint
5ff07638, Python reference engine, GB10): instant decisions 4/28 units, reasoned 26/28, Luna 56/56; instant gave
`billing` for every spam ticket and P(urgent) 0.89-0.91 on every ticket; the calibration hunt (10 record prompts,
sft-v8) found instant agreeing with reasoned on 7-8/10.

**Cause.** The instant readout scores each option right after the empty think block (`<think></think>` + option +
`<|im_end|>`, `decision_items`; `</think>` is shared, so prompt). 5ff07638 does not answer there: after `</think>` it
opens a tool call (greedy `<tool_call>` on all 56 readouts; p 0.97 on the spam ticket probed); the bare value's first token gets ~e^-8 (`"`) and
`true`/`false` e^-13/e^-15. Among those improbable continuations what separates the options is not the ticket:
- urgency: `true` beats `false` by 1.96-2.49 nats on all 28 tickets (input-independent: P(urgent) 0.89-0.91);
- label: `"spam"` is tokenized `"sp`+`am` (canonical BPE of the rendered reply) while `"billing"` is `"`+`b`+`illing`;
  `"sp` costs ~10 nats there, so the first-listed `billing` wins every spam ticket (billing and technical tickets were
  labelled right: 17/28 labels).
The same model in `{"result": VALUE}` (the existing stock-model frame) reads the tickets: 26/28 units on the exact B14
prompts (classify 26, is_urgent 28/28), as many as reasoned. The calibration hunt did not collapse because its readouts
were records (`{"label":...}`): the shared `{"` opening is prompt, so the fields are scored where the model writes JSON,
and sft-v8 was trained on bare-value readout rows. 5ff07638 is not stock LFM3 either: its checkpoint is a
`natlang.neuralese-native-sft-training/1` save (whole-trajectory teacher-program rows), the one the machine's stale
`lfm-latest` profile still serves (current-policy is sft-v6 dc95f29d); B14 labels it "base".

Evidence (scratchpad scripts, per-ticket JSON: `/home/werg/data/semantic-fp-bench/triage-instant-20261123/evidence/`):
the exact readout request captured through a logging proxy (`natlang call` on the llama.cpp fork, CPU, same checkpoint
as GGUF Q8_0) reproduced `billing` for a spam ticket; per-token log-probs of every option; the same 28 tickets scored in
both forms on the fork (value 4/28 units, P(urgent) 0.84-0.96; object 26/28, P(urgent) 0.00-1.00); the trained
contrast on aei1's collection policy e15b20a8 (Colab SGLang front): after `</think>` the bare value holds ~all of the
mass (log-sum -0.00 vs -0.2 for the object), value 21/28, object 18/28 (its 7 instant misses are spam -> billing: its
no-reasoning answer; reasoning fixes them).

**Engines (ruled out).** Python native (bench traces) vs llama.cpp fork on the 56 B14 readouts: argmax 56/56, TV mean
0.005 (max 0.036); the per-option shift between them is the fork build's unshared `</think>` (median spread 0.29 nats).
The collapse is the model at that position, not an engine. SGLang was compared on a different checkpoint only (the
Colab front serves e15b20a8), not on 5ff07638.

**Fix (defaults, opt-outs, tests).**
- `decisionReply: 'auto'` is the default of every profile but a managed stock model (that keeps `result-object`):
  a joint readout without reasoning is scored in both forms and each option alone; the form whose lone scores sum to
  more probability is read (`decision-frame.ts` `autoFramedScores`, one round of 2+2K items; trace `reply_frame`,
  `reply_masses`). Opt-outs: profile `decisionReply: 'value'`, `NATLANG_DECISION_REPLY=value`. On the fork mirror of
  the rule (`auto_eval.py`): 5ff07638 26/28 units (the object form chosen on 56/56 readouts); e15b20a8 21/28 (value
  on 55/56 readouts: unchanged).
- Reasoning samples are drawn at the call's temperature, else T=1 (`decisionReasoningTemperature`): with none set they
  took the backend default, greedy on the native engine, so B14's C-reasoned drew the same reasoning 4 times (identical
  texts and conditionals in the traces): 4x the decode for one draw, and a floor read one conditional. Opt-out
  `NATLANG_DECISION_REASONING_TEMPERATURE=backend`.
- Inventory of the reply-form mechanism: `model/local-server.ts` decide (managed llama-server, external endpoints and
  the native engine and SGLang front behind them, all through `createResolvedModelSession`), `browser/local-model.ts`
  (in-page engine: it applied no frame at all, so the stock page model was read in the bare value; now `auto`). Not
  applicable: Pi providers (no scorer, `local-server.ts` decide throws `decision-unsupported`); the engines (the form
  is the request's messages and options, rendered by each engine as any item); the learner: decision rows are built
  from the recorded turn (`sft_sources` decision rows read `decision_graph.decision_replies(messages)`, the runtime's
  bare-value request, target the chosen value), so training keeps teaching the bare value and captures record what was
  scored. Not changed here: the Vibestudio gateway driver (`@workspace/natlang`, another repository) frames with its own
  setting.

**Found, not changed.** Canonical tokenization of an option (`"sp`+`am`) is not the model's own (it writes `"`,
`spam`, `"` when it generates); on e15b20a8, which was trained on canonical rows, splitting at the options' shared
characters lowered value-form instant from 21 to 18/28, and it splits ` true` into ` `+`true` in the object form, so
neither tokenization is right for every model: summing both tokenizations per option is the exact fix and needs an
item field on all four engines and the learner (open).

**Re-measure (bench.py, C-instant, same program 19844f4d + this commit's runtime, 5ff07638 native, 28 held units).**
Runtime: the build of b1340c3e7's change on b0fe8d310 (the bench started before the rebase; the dist was kept),
work dir `/home/werg/data/semantic-fp-bench/triage-instant-20261123` (evidence/ holds the offline scripts and data).
- after (default `auto`): **23/28** (0.821, unit-bootstrap CI [0.68, 0.96]); label 0.82, urgency 0.93; every readout

  7.94, reasoned 3.28; 37.6 busy GPU-s/unit). vs B14 C-instant: +67.9 pts, CI [+42.9, +89.3], permutation p 0.0001,
  21 units better, 2 worse; vs B14 C-reasoned: -10.7 pts, CI [-25.0, +3.6], p 0.37 (4 vs 1 units).
  Misses: 3 spam tickets labelled billing (loans, mortgage refinance, translation services) and 2 urgent units whose
  `natlang run` exited 0 with non-JSON stdout (both readouts and the summary were right in their traces; a rerun of
  one printed the correct report; cause not established: bench.py now keeps such stdout in the unit).
- before (the same runtime with `NATLANG_DECISION_REPLY=value`): B14's 4/28 stands as the baseline. The opt-out run
  reproduced B14 unit for unit on the 5 units it finished (same labels, P(urgent) 0.88-0.92, the same 2 passes) and was

**Not checked.** SGLang on 5ff07638; the bench on the policy (arm D); the in-page engine end to end (unit test of the
wrapper only); field-by-field record readouts under `auto` (they keep the bare value); other checkpoints' preferred

e15b20a8; C-reasoned after the T=1 change (its result moves: reasoning is now sampled); whether the stale `lfm-latest`

## 2026-11-23 16:30 Reference engine: memory-bounded admission, busy-tolerant supervision; lfm-latest = sft-v9; B14 triage rerun

**Observations (B14, DECISIONS "B14 flagship benchmark harness").** The Python reference engine OOMed at its CUDA cap
(9 GB policy server, 4 concurrent `natlang call`s: 10 OOMs in 7 min, all 74-92 MiB allocations with 8.0-8.3 GB
allocated), and `natlang serve` killed it after one 10 s health timeout (14:27). Every `natlang call` then found no
answer at the port and launched its own duplicate server (two ledger launchers for the same unit, the queue head at
18.9 GB for 35 min), which left arm D's driver stalled on old code. Stopped: `d-driver.sh` (PID 860045),
`bench-prepd-8`, the stale queued `natlang-native-dc95f29dd5a0-18471` claim.

**Fixes (41fa2c044, a2ecee97f; default on, opt-out `--unbounded-admission`).**
- Admission (`serve/engine.py`): queued requests wait in a FIFO and join the batch only while the running batch's
  worst-case KV (bytes per token measured from finished prefills' caches, buffer headroom included, x prompt + remaining
  allowance clamped to the context), the largest measured prefill workspace and the prefix cache's unspent budget fit
  both the `--memory-gb` cap and the device's free memory, minus a 10% watermark; the oldest always runs; cancelled
  waiters leave the queue. An OOM prefill that produced nothing is requeued as a fresh sequence (same request and seed)
  while others run, and fails alone. Metrics: waiting, deferrals, OOM requeues, measured bytes/token and workspace.
  Engine parity: llama-server admits by fixed slots, SGLang by its KV pool, wllama serves one sequence; only the
  reference engine was unbounded.
- Supervision: `natlang serve` ends only when the port stops listening (TCP connect; the kernel completes the
  handshake for a process too busy to answer); an unanswered /health logs "busy" and keeps serving. A command that finds
  a listening but unanswering server at its port waits instead of launching a duplicate; `natlang status` says `busy`.
  Same flaw on the managed llama-server path: the shared supervisor counted an unanswered `/slots` as idle (could stop a
  busy server once leases lapsed) and an acquirer that saw a live record fail /health started a second server; both
  fixed. SGLang is not launched by `natlang serve` (`serveCommand` requires `managedNative`; `nativeServerCommand` always
  runs `natlang_neuralese.serve`), so it has no such supervisor.
- `natlang build`/`check` of a program outside a checkout resolves `@natlang/node/std` to the CLI's declarations (the
  bench's copy of triage failed TS2307 after it began importing `escalate`/`semanticRepair`).
- Health route: it never touched the engine (shown by a test with a blocked engine thread). The stall's root cause is
  not established; under the rerun's load the probe answered 1,206/1,206 within 0.57 s (max), with 0 deferrals and 0
  OOM requeues at concurrency 4 (7 active sequences peak, 4.4 GB allocated, 153.6 KB/token measured).

**lfm-latest = sft-v9 (coordinator).** `ops/current-policy.json` now names sft-v9 (e15b20a86f1c, ops/ei/sft-v9/sft):
