**What happened (06:20, corrected by hand 06:25).** `phase-state.json`'s `reference_policy` was sft-v7 (9ebc8799)
while the driver's `--reference`/`--reference-sha` named sft-v9 (e15b20a8). `PhaseController.initialize` returns
the stored state as it is, so the stored value won silently. Held verdicts were queued against sft-v7. The held loop
reused an old sft-v7 result of another engine series, `held_eval compare` refused the pair, and the verdict failed
every 5 minutes.

**Rule (`PhaseController.reconcile_arguments`, at every driver start).** The state moves some values on by itself;
the arguments seed them. So an argument is adopted unless the loop's own record shows it moved the value on, and
an argument that would change the experiment's identity is refused:
- `--start`: one that differs from the loop's start (`start_policy`, recorded now; for older states the lineage's
  version-0 entry) refuses with a message. Another start is another experiment: use a fresh `--root`.
- `--reference`/`--reference-sha`: the stored reference is kept only when a held verdict adopted it (a history
  `adopt` of that sha). Otherwise the argument is adopted, and an open measurement's reference is re-pointed at it.
- `--held-every`/`--held-every-max` set the base interval and its cap (the current interval follows a base change
  and is clamped to the cap). `--prefer-unseen` entries missing from the state are added. `--initial-phase` applies
  only to a new state (the phase is the loop's).
- Each change goes to `history` (`action: arguments`) and to the driver log (`arguments_reconciled`).

**Held pairs.**
- `Cycle.compare` raises `HeldPairRefused` when `held_eval compare` refuses a pairing (engine settings, sampling
  law, budget, host).
- `judge_measurement` then sets the reference's result aside (`<name>-unpaired-<time>`) and measures it again on
  this series without reuse (`measure_held(..., reuse=False)`). If the pair is refused again it does the same for
  the candidate. A third refusal raises, a real fault.

Tests (`tests/neuralese/test_async_train.py`): the sft-v7/sft-v9 case, a kept verdict-adopted reference, the start
refusal (recorded and inferred), interval and prefer-unseen adoption, a restarted driver adopting its argument; the
refused pair re-measuring the reference without reuse, the raise after both were re-measured, other compare failures
not taken for refusals.

## 2026-11-24 07:40 The SGLang front's single-process ceiling: whole-reply detokenization per chunk, a cold-start tokenizer herd, a 1024-fd limit; fixed in one process (no worker split)

**Brief.** Raise aei1's collection throughput by removing the native front's single-process (one GIL) ceiling: measure
where its time goes at production concurrency, fix the `Errno 24 Too many open files` seen before the 03:04 OOM kill of
`aei1-collect-v0001`, remove the ceiling by the mechanism the profile points to.

**Live production (before), aei1-collect-v0002 on pin a034dbf9c, 128 slots, 04:44-04:46.** Front 0.97 cores,
1,556 tok/s through it (60 s of `/metrics` counters), 0.62 ms of front CPU per generated token; SGLang at 158-160
running (its `--sglang-max-running 160`, shared with the fill) with 2-30 queued, 1,250-2,330 tok/s in all;
`/metrics` answered in 1-47 ms. 257 sockets open at 128 streams (one client and one SGLang connection per stream) under
the unit's soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` of 1024 (hard 500000). Production rate of that run: 45 groups, 174 episodes from 04:22
to its 05:21 preemption by `aei1-r0003-build` (~175 episodes/h). py-spy cannot attach to the live front (ptrace scope 1,
the front is not our child, no sudo), so the front was measured on a bench instead of being signalled.

**Bench** (`benchmarks/sglang-front/`, run on the Colab A100 VM's CPUs as a preemptible admission beside r0003's SFT,
because the DGX ledger had no room): the front built as `serve_native_checkpoint.py` builds it (checkpoint 7cfc4774,
its SGLang export, tool grammar on), bound to a mock SGLang that replays 687 recorded aei1 v0002 turns (122 episodes,
738k tokens) with their per-token records in 8-token chunks at a set rate per stream; 128 streaming chat clients
replay the episodes; py-spy as the front's parent (`--gil`). 0 mock misses: every request's prompt matched its recording.

**Where the time went (py-spy, GIL-holding samples).**
1. Cold start: 87-90% in `tool_grammar.info_from_export` -> `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` (~3 s of GIL-held Python
   each). lru_cache and f29b9cd43's per-export cache do not stop concurrent first callers from each building it, so every
   stream's first request after a start loaded the tokenizer: 4 requests reached SGLang in the first 150 s at 32
   streams.
2. Steady state: `_sglang_emit` decoded the whole reply so far at every 8-token chunk (quadratic in the reply
   length): 57% of the GIL samples at 32 streams, 79% at 128 (`TokenizersBackend._decode` and transformers' `to_py_obj`
   over the id list). Next: `_sglang_consume` record decoding 6-9%, the HTTP stream's event JSON 4-7%, append-only
   hashing ~5%. The tool grammar itself is cheap: 0.9 us per accepted token, 0.17 s per new tool set (24 sets in 687
   turns), cached after.

**Fixes** (each default on with an opt-out and tests; main commits below).
- Streamed text: `_sglang_emit` decodes the previous chunk plus the new tokens and sends what that adds to the previous
  chunk's decode (vLLM's prefix/read offsets, which keeps a tokenizer's inter-token spacing); an incomplete UTF-8 tail
  waits, a context that is not a prefix falls back to the whole decode, and the run's final emission still decodes the
  reply whole. The 687 recorded replies stream to exactly their whole decode both ways (2.6 s against 75 s of CPU).
  `NATLANG_SGLANG_INCREMENTAL_DETOKENIZE=0` opts out.
- Tokenizer info: `tool_grammar.INFO_LOCK` makes `info_from_export`/`info_from_base` and both engines'
  `_tool_grammar_info` single-flight, and `serve_native_checkpoint` builds it before the server starts.
- Open files: `common/open_files.raise_open_files_limit` (soft to hard; `NATLANG_RAISE_NOFILE=0` opts out) in
  `serve/http.serve` (every Python engine), `expert_iteration` and `run_bonsai_queue` (their node workers inherit it).
  Connection pooling was not added: an open stream holds its sockets either way, and front -> SGLang requests run at
  ~1.3/s, so connection setup is no cost. The pile-up that reached 1024 in v0001 (likely retried streams whose first
  attempt kept running during the stalled-front period) was not reconstructed.

**Throughput, bench (steady state 60 s .. end-30 s, mock served tokens; 128 streams).**

| front | demand (tok/s) | tok/s | front cores | CPU ms/token | /metrics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a034dbf9c (before) | 5,120 | 4,054 (front-bound) | 1.42 | 0.352 | 0.9-1.7 s |
| this change | 5,120 | 5,074 (demand-bound) | 0.82 | 0.162 | 9-15 ms |
| this change | 12,800 | 8,284 (front-bound) | 1.62 | 0.195 | 0.2-0.7 s |

The single front's ceiling rose from ~4.0k to ~8.3k tok/s on the VM's cores (2.0x, and the before front could not meet
5.1k). DGX cores ran the production front at 0.62 ms/token against the VM's 0.35 for the same code (slower cores,
load 70-85), which puts the DGX front's new ceiling near 4.5k tok/s, about twice what SGLang decodes on the GB10 at 160
running. Episodes per hour on the bench are not comparable to production (recorded tool output, no node workers); the
production before/after in episodes/h and tok/s is read at the next collection start on the new pin.

**No worker split.** One front per ~64 streams would need SGLang adapter-slot partitioning between processes, rebind
and attestation fan-out, owner/episode affinity for the exclusive native-state store and append-only histories, and a
lazily loaded native model per worker (~14 GB each on a fallback). With the front no longer the bound that buys nothing
now; revisit if SGLang decode passes ~4k tok/s on the DGX or the front's CPU per token rises again.

**For aei1 (coordinator).** Take the pin at the next round boundary. Slots can rise now, together with SGLang's
running cap, which binds first (160 running with requests queued, KV pool 56% used): e.g. `--slots 192` with
`--actor-arg=--sglang-max-running --actor-arg=224`; keep it if SGLang's gen throughput rises by >= 10% in the first
progress lines, else return to 128/160.

**Inventory.** Streaming detokenization: the SGLang front (fixed); the native engine's `Engine._emit` decodes only the
pending token(s) (`serve/engine.py` `_emit`); guided replies publish through `native_guidance.flush` and never call
`_sglang_emit` (`_sglang_consume`, `_sglang_feed_forced`: `seq.guide is None`); llama-server and the page detokenize
per token in llama.cpp. Tokenizer info: `tool_grammar` (both builders), `Engine` and `SglangEngine._tool_grammar_info`
(fixed); llama-server/wllama compile grammars in C++. Open files: Python servers and collectors (fixed); node raises its
soft limit to the hard one itself (a live collector: 500000); the SGLang server sets 65535 itself (live process).

**After the change, at its ceiling** (py-spy `--gil --nonblocking`, 128 streams, 8.0k tok/s): the GIL time spreads
over the grammar matcher's per-token `accept_token` (20%; 0.9 us per token uncontended, so mostly the FFI call's GIL
release and retake among ~130 busy threads), reading SGLang's chunked stream (12%), the client stream's event JSON and
writes (13%), append-only prompt hashing (8%) and record decoding (~4%). None dominates; batching the matcher calls per
chunk is the next lever if the front binds again.

**Not checked.** The new front on DGX cores under production load (read at the next start); the per-token residue
above was left as is; the exact sequence behind v0001's 1024 descriptors.

## 2026-11-24 10:30 The teacher campaign is a standing queue of every teacher-eligible task, routed by measured yield

**Observed (09:30).** Each campaign took `--limit` = the newest frontier's rare-task count: 234 for r0002, then 46
(r0004) and 41 (r0005) once `--snapshot-min-hours` went from 2 to 1. A campaign ended in ~30 min, and its 24 slots sat
idle until the next frontier, ~2 h. The frontier only set the count. teacher_gen took the first N tasks of its own gap
order, and 38 of r0005's 41 frontier-rare tasks already had a teacher success. Gemini Argon (`min_failed: 1`) had 3
episodes, because few tasks in a 41-task campaign were teacher-failed. Measured yields (all manifests, Luna and Sol):
aei1 student-rare tasks with no prior teacher failure 10/24 (42%), with three prior failures 7/242 (3%); fresh
unmeasured tasks (`teacher_untried`) Luna 178/371 (48%), Sol 109/190 (57%). Nemotron Ultra and Super scored 0/99 on the
aei1 student-rare tasks and ERNIE 0/23 overall.

**Decision (built; opt-out `async-drive --no-standing-teacher`).**
- **Standing queue.** `ensure_teacher` launches the newest frontier's campaign with `--limit 0`: the whole ordered
  queue. Rates come from the newest collection's `tasks.rates.json` (every collection, newest first), then the lineage
  groups, then the frontier; the newest measurement wins (`teacher_gen --student-rates/--frontier-rates`). When a
  newer frontier appears, the running campaign gets `WORK/DRAIN`: its running episodes finish, it takes no new task
  and exits. The driver checks every minute while a drain is pending and launches the re-prioritised queue (earlier
  campaigns cover their successes). Exclusions are unchanged: held-v3/v2/v4 closure via `grpo.load_tasks`,
  `ops/pool-errata`, and teacher-covered tasks.
- **Order by expected value** (`GAP_TIERS`):
  1. `student_rare`: rate <= 0.25 and no teacher failed it.
  2. `priority_pool`.
  3. `student_band`: rate between 0.25 and 0.9, where a teacher success adds a solved variant.
  4. `teacher_untried`: unmeasured.
  5. `teacher_failed`.
  6. `student_rare_failed`: last, at 3% yield.

  Tasks the student solves >= 0.9 are left out. Within a tier, fewer teacher failures come first, family round-robin.
  A dry run at 10:20 on r0005's inputs gave 7,442 queued tasks: 29 / 0 / 44 / 5,429 / 1,882 / 58. Of the
  `teacher_failed` tasks, 1,777 have three failures.
- **Routing by measured yield.** A teacher's strength is its posterior yield on `teacher_untried` verdicts (all
  covered campaigns, 5 episodes of prior at 0.3). A teacher below `--weak-yield 0.25` never takes the student-rare
  tiers. A failure there spends one of the task's attempts and demotes it for every later campaign. Today that means
  Nemotron Ultra (0.19), Nemotron Super (0.16) and ERNIE (0.07); Luna, Sol and the Gemini models are strong.
  - Each teacher takes the first queue task it may take, so strong teachers take the hard tiers first. Family routing
    (`--route-ratio`, `--route-floor`) is unchanged.
  - A task a teacher fails here stays at its queue position for the next teacher. That feeds Luna's fresh failures to
    Sol and Gemini (`min_failed: 1`, kept as configured) ahead of the three-times-failed backlog.
  - Each launch logs a `teacher routing` line per teacher: fresh yield, episodes, weak, min_failed, slots.
- **Rate limits.** Unchanged: per-teacher provider cooldowns, deferral and retirement on a refused account. A task
  deferred three times is done for the launch, instead of being re-taken.

**Expected.** About 350-500 episodes/h and 100-170 successes/h (estimate):
- Luna: 6 slots x 60-90 s.
- Sol and Gemini: on failed tasks.
- Previously: ~44 successes/h while running, less with the idle gaps.

The Codex subscription limit at a sustained Luna+Sol rate is not measured. Gemini's Vertex spend rises from ~3
episodes per campaign to its 6 slots busy; the owner is deciding that spend (`ops/ei/teachers.json` slots).

## 2026-11-24 10:00 Held reuse never takes a set-aside result; a running measurement is joined, its directory never moved

**What happened at the 09:41 restart (pin 89ebbf2a3).**
1. `reuse_held` copied the reference result from `held/policy-e15b20a86f1c-unpaired-1795501815`, which the previous
   driver had set aside as unpaired.
2. The pair was refused again, and `set_held_aside` moved the whole directory to
   `policy-e15b20a86f1c-unpaired-1795509710`. A Pop re-measurement had been writing into that directory since 07:41
   (`popheld-policy-e15b20a86f1c-1795502476`).
3. The unit failed at 09:42 (`FileNotFoundError: .../packet.jsonl`). Its episodes (row-000..255, run.json) are in
   the aside directory.

**Fix (e771e3673's re-measure path).**
- **Never reused:** `held_reuse_candidates` excludes any result in a set-aside directory (`aside.json`, or named
  `<name>-<reason>-<epoch>`). Into the series that refused a result, it also excludes that result's bytes and the
  source it was reused from.
- **What a set-aside records:** `set_held_aside` writes `aside.json` (reason, series host and key, result sha256,
  `reused_from`).
- **Only the result moves:** a reused result, or a result in a directory a measurement unit still writes into, moves
  alone (`result.json`, `reused.json`). The measurement's files stay where it writes them.
- **Joined:** `pop_held` joins a running `popheld-<OUT>-*` unit before it considers reuse, and `dgx_held` skips the
  result check and reuse while its unit runs (`held_measuring`).

Test: `tests/neuralese/test_async_train.py` covers this sequence.

journal looked silent). Not a tenant fault: the program-tuning fit tenant ran outside MPS beside nothing.

Fix (1b88e5d3f, default, tests in `test_colab_session_keeper.py` and `test_colab_and_profiles.py`): a yield moves the
record to `colab-actor-<host>.yielded.json`; `restore_colab_actor` removes it only after a successful restore; a
`run-sft` restarted mid-round adopts it; the keeper treats "yielded record, no live record, no round on the session" as
actor down and serves it from that record (beside the earlier `pending_serve` retry and dead-actor checks). The actor
was served at 1823ce9b at 10:00:18 through the keeper's pending-serve path; both keepers run from `/home/werg/natlang`.

The free-tier runs on pin 6263a970f were stopped and rerun on eb31c6f4a after the decide() fix below (their first runs
lost every decide() call to a 400).

**Harness bug found and fixed (eb31c6f4a): hosted teachers' decide().** The prompt-scoring request a decision readout
sends (`promptLogprobDecider`) carried every collection control except max_tokens/temperature/stream, so the
client-side `x_natlang_*` controls reached the server: NIM 400 "Unsupported parameter(s): x_natlang_history_reasoning"
(188 failed calls in one Lightning run), AI Studio 400 "Unknown name x_natlang_omit_seed" (Vertex accepts unknown top-level fields, so its "Expected a
valid JSON object" decide() 400 of the 01:00 entry is a refusal of the scoring request itself, not proven to be the
leak; both now fall back). And a hosted server that refuses `prompt_logprobs` itself (400/404/422)
failed the call instead of falling back to generated decisions (only a missing `prompt_logprobs` field did). Now
`CLIENT_REQUEST_CONTROLS` are stripped from every scoring request (and the explicit-batch scorer's `request`), and a
4xx other than 408/429 is `decision-unsupported`: the runtime reads that function's decisions by generation (verified
on Flash-Lite: `decision_readout unavailable decision-unsupported`, then generated). Inventory: requests built from the
collection controls are `chatCompletionModelTurn` (strips them), `promptLogprobDecider` and `explicitBatchScoreMany`
(fixed); the Pi provider path takes provider controls, not these; engines are receivers. Production impact so far:
1 Nemotron episode in r0001, none found in r0005; but r0005's pin (23a358778fd3) has the NIM `x_natlang_history_reasoning`
default and not the fix: its NIM teachers' decide() calls fail until the campaign moves to a pin >= eb31c6f4a.

## 2026-11-24 aei1 driver: health report off the loop, SFT launch retries, standing remote collectors, ledger backoff head

Four defects seen between 09:50 and 10:35:

1. **The health report blocked the main loop.** `health_report` read every earlier collection's groups, including
   v0000's 45k files tiered to the HDD (about 350 ms each), and held r0005's SFT launch for 25 min. The fix:
   - It now runs in a thread beside the loop (`start_health_report`, one at a time).
   - Earlier collections come only from `health-cache`: a closed whole summary, or else the scored groups an older
     cache holds. A collection without a cache is listed under `collections.uncached` and never read.
   - The previous policy's collections are finished when the report runs and still on the NVMe, so the report closes
     their caches (`collection_summary(close=True)`).

   The same read pattern was in `select` (`tasks.json`), which globbed every collection's groups. It now takes the
   newest earlier collection's `tasks.rates.json` (`--rates-json`, every outcome up to that selection) plus the
   lineage collections and `r*/grpo`. The loop's first selection still reads every collection. The frontier and the
   teacher queue already read only the lineage (current and previous) collections and `tasks.rates.json`. The build
   reads the lineage collections, `r*/grpo` and `teacher-*`. Both match the `ei_round_tier` assumption.
2. **A failed `launch-sft.sh` ended the driver.** The preflight unit (4 GB, low, `--wait 600`) was not admitted, and
   the resulting `CalledProcessError` ended the driver. The fix:
   - `launch_sft` now notes each failure (`sft_launch_failed`, `attempt`) and retries after 60 s, doubling to 15 min.
   - Between attempts it keeps the remote collectors and the teacher running.
   - It stops retrying once a DGX learner of the round runs.
   - The round env sets `PREFLIGHT_PRIORITY=high` and `PREFLIGHT_WAIT=3600`, which the coordinator's edit of the ops
     script reads.

   `launch-sft.sh` stays in ops: its preflight (`ops/grpo-v4/sft_preflight.py`) and the legacy cycle use it there, and
   the driver now dictates the preflight's priority and wait itself.
3. **Remote collectors started only at a round's start and in the DGX SFT's polls.** The A100 actor came back at 10:00
   and got no collector until a 10:20 restart. A standing thread (`remote_collect_loop`, every 5 min, in the SFT phase)
   now starts a collector for every reachable actor that serves the newest policy. While a round's Colab SFT trains on
   a session, no actor is rebound, but serving actors still get collectors. The opt-out is
   `--no-standing-remote-collection`. Collector starts are serialized (`REMOTE_LOCK`).
4. **The ledger's low queue was stuck.** The head `vibe-student-fill-1795481059079952364` had been preempted three
   times within 30 min of each relaunch (09:32, 09:44 and 10:00, by medium jobs), so its requeue backoff doubled to
   1920 s. Its 10:32:39 relaunch is exactly 10:00:35 + 1920 s. For that whole backoff it stayed head of the low queue,
   and a low job behind it could start only as a "spare" backfill: both needs free, each 4 GB plus the 15 GB DGX
   reserve, about 38 GB against 28-31 GB free. The fix in `memory_ledger.py`:
   - Within one priority, a requeued unit still in its backoff queues behind eligible jobs. A higher-priority unit in
     backoff still precedes every lower one.
   - A preemption (a stop for a waiting higher job, not for the unit's own memory) caps the backoff at 10 min.

   The 238 stale `waiting` entries (since 2026-10-12, `seen` never refreshed) did not matter: `waiting_order` ignores
   them after `WAITER_TTL`. The guard now drops non-requeued ones unrefreshed for an hour (`prune_stale_waiting`).

   **The memory guard (`natlang-memory-guard`) runs from `/home/werg/natlang` and picks this up only after a pull and
   a restart.**
- **Drive tier lost most of its uplink to preemption (2026-11-24 11:20).** Over 3 h at the 5 MiB/s setting, Drive gained
  only 5.8 GB, although uploads in flight ran at 5.3 MiB/s.
  - The cause: the ledger preempted the low-priority resumable unit 24 times in 17 h, for medium jobs, while it held
    0.0-0.4 GB. Each preemption discarded a multi-GB upload in flight.
  - Second cause: the pass deadline gated only the start of a file, so a 4 GB upload begun late was killed by the
    unit timeout.
  - Fix: the unit now runs at medium priority and is not preemptible (1 GB budget). A file starts only if it can
    finish at 3 MiB/s before `--hard-minutes` (54, under the 55-minute timeout); otherwise smaller files fill the
    pass. Test added.
- **EI round tier stalled (2026-11-24 11:30): fixed.** After 09:48 the tier moved nothing while root fell from 102 to
  65 GB.
  - Cause: its first move, `collect/v0002` (13.25 GB), never finished. One pass was OOM-killed in the sweep's 1 GB
    cgroup (dirty HDD writeback counts against it), one was preempted, and one hit the 1200 s step timeout. Each
    retry started by deleting `.partial`.
  - Fix in `copy_tree_verified`:
    - it resumes from `.partial`, reusing files whose size and mtime_ns equal the source's (digest from the NVMe
      source; every file is still re-read from disk and compared);
    - it syncs and drops each 64 MB written;
    - a file that fails verification is removed.
  - The sweep unit is now medium, not preemptible, at 3 GB. Tests added.

## 2026-11-24 Live CPU collection can release a fixed reservation without changing its cap

Inventory: `scripts/memory_ledger.py` owns `fixed_claim`, `outstanding`, `adopt`, managed restart specs and the admission/pressure guard; all engines and collectors use that same allocator. `run --hold-budget` pins unspent allowance even after startup; `adopt` preserved it unconditionally, so a ready CPU collection could not switch to the standard measured-headroom policy without a restart. The V21 teacher's fixed 13 GiB plus a 6 GiB native claim and 7.5 GiB reserve exceeds actual available memory slightly, despite actual steady use fitting. Do not lower caps or the reserve. Add explicit `adopt --release-fixed-claim` to resume ordinary CPU headroom accounting, preserve MemoryMax/restart/ownership, and record the transition. Default re-adoption still preserves the fixed claim. The active Tick guard (7.5 GiB floor, 4 GiB emergency floor, 2-second interval) protects the host and can retire the resumable low-priority native work if real pressure develops; the teacher remains at 13 GiB and native at 6 GiB. No engine-specific allocator implementation is left out.


## 2026-11-24 Graceful ledger preemption signals the owning process before its children

Actual native single-context work was stopped at 11:33:53 for a medium-priority Android-tail quick check, not OOM (5 GiB peak below 6 GiB; physical available 11.5 GiB). A 90-second grace was ineffective: shared `memory_ledger.terminate` used `systemctl kill --signal=SIGTERM UNIT`, whose default scope includes every child. The owner lost its CLI/server/workerd before it could export completed in-memory results. Existing 98 completed packets remain intact.

Inventory: `terminate` is the shared guard stop path for pressure and priority preemption (one caller in `guard`); container TERM already targets the container main process. Final `kill`/survivor sweep intentionally target all remaining processes. Other scripts' `Popen.terminate` target their owned child PID, not a systemd cgroup. Make graceful systemd TERM explicitly `--kill-whom=main` (supported on Tick and DGX); preserve final hard cleanup. `guard --terminate-cgroup` opts back into all-process TERM for diagnosis. Native controller checkpoint/export also needs to respect its declared grace. Code checks use low priority so they do not preempt useful work. Serving engines, learner and collectors all consume this shared allocator stop mechanism rather than implementing a second one.

`success_rate` 0.637 was 293/460 and the adopted verdict (+4.47 pts, p 0.05) came from `compare`, which left each
side's unscored episodes out of that side only, so the reference (sft-v9, 512/512 scored) kept its outcomes on the
52 tasks-samples the candidate lost.

Cause (from the journals, worker error files and Pop's user journal): all 52 are infrastructure losses, in three
clusters where every in-flight episode failed within seconds. 01:56:37 the Pop actor unit was stopped under a running
measurement (a second held start re-served it, the double start 1afe6e8aa fixed): 20 episodes, 0 model calls.
02:52:33 and 05:47:57 the SGLang engine exited with code 70 (`ENGINE_DIED_EXIT`) and `pop_actor_driver` relaunched it
within a minute: 17 and 15 in-flight episodes failed with `ProviderRequestRetriesExhaustedError ... ECONNREFUSED`.
Four more were scored as budget failures because ts-host counted the resends of failed requests against the 40-call
budget (episodes at 37-39 calls; s7-task-092-01, 119-00, 161-01, 211-01). Defects: (1) `collect` skipped every
finished episode on resume, so lost ones were never re-run; (2) `classify_case` read a result-less episode whose
provider request exhausted its resends as `unresolved`, not `infrastructure_error`; (3) `compare`/`paired`/
`task_counts`, `result.json`'s `success_rate` and the dashboard dropped all unscored episodes per side; (4) the
collector's resends consumed model-call budget.

Mechanism inventory: episode outcome (`eval/task_packet.classify_case`, used by training rewards and held alike);
request budget (`ts-host/src/teacher/collector.ts`, the one collector behind every engine); held measurement
(`rl/held_eval.py` collect/finalize/aggregate/merge, used by `grpo.py` held, `expert_iteration` DGX and Pop held,
`pop-held.sh`); verdict (`held_eval.compare`, `expert_iteration.judge_measurement`/`verdict_stage`); views
(`ops_dashboard/ei_export.held_record`/`paired`, `views.mjs`). Left out: training pass rates for selection
(`expert_iteration.group_outcomes`, `grpo.py` 745/1024) exclude every unscored episode; they are frontier weights,
not verdicts, and their rows carry no loss classification (the classifier fix applies to them).

Changes (default on, opt-outs named): `held_eval.infra_loss` labels a loss (scorer `infrastructure_error`, or a
call-budget stop whose evidence shows a provider resend); `collect` re-runs lost episodes from scratch in passes after
the main one and on resume, at most `INFRA_ATTEMPTS` = 3 attempts (files set aside to `sample-NN.lost-K`;
`rerun_lost=False` opts out); samples carry `infra_lost`/`lost_attempts`; `success_rate` is over `counted` (ran, not
lost) episodes with `infra_lost`/`counted` fields; `compare` leaves a lost (task, sample) out of both sides and counts
every other unscored episode as a failure (timeouts too in the primary), reports `pairs_lost_to_infrastructure` and
warns; `held_eval relabel DIR --out FILE` labels an older result again without touching DIR. `classify_case` labels a
result-less transport failure `infrastructure_error`. The collector counts a resent request once
(`NATLANG_BUDGET_EACH_RESEND=1` restores counting each resend). The verdict records carry
`pairs_lost_to_infrastructure`; the dashboard pairs by the same rule. New scoring series (task_packet, ts-host tree).

Re-judgement (relabel of both results, fixed compare, 2000 and 20000 resamples): 56 candidate pairs left out of both
sides; reference 266/456 vs candidate 293/456; mean per-task change +5.49 pts (246 tasks, 57.9% -> 63.4%), CI
[+0.8, +10.4], permutation p 0.025; McNemar 38:65 p 0.010, tasks 48 up / 29 down (sign p 0.040); ran-out -4.3 pts.
The success verdict (>= +2 pts, ran-out <= +2) holds. For reference: counting the 56 as failures gives -0.2 pts

## 2026-11-24: repair program-owned service scope ancestry

The actual Vibe teacher failures exposed scoped services missing from NL calls even though the TS coordinator's service calls worked. The shared kernel mixed program/context-qualified recursion identity into the raw authored source service chain; native service lookup also consulted ambient context instead of its own invocation frame. Repair both exact plumbing boundaries as the default, retaining original service-scope declarations and program/context recursion ownership. No training, model call, full native sweep or live Source mutation gates the repair; the supervising runtime strand owns downstream SDK staging and next-pin activation. Tests use explicit program IDs, bound contexts, mixed TS/NL descendants and negative sibling scopes under Node/workerd platforms with a deterministic agent callback. Original Workerd OOM attribution remains open and independent.

## 2026-11-24 Ops dashboard: page signals lost for 4.5 h to phone clock drift; the stale alert separates link from exporter

Observed: from 09:50Z the owner's page sent no query or telemetry that reached `ops-peer-25`. Its commands still arrived, and the
peer's connection flapped every 10-30 s. A peer restart (ops-peer-26) did not help. Cause: the phone's clock drifted ahead of the DGX
by ~0.1 s/h (0.37 s on 11-23 18:23Z, 1.97 s on 11-24 09:43Z, from the page telemetry's `at` against peer receive time) and crossed
Chronolog's default `maxClockSkewMs` of 2 s at about 09:50Z. The receiver throws `SIGNAL_CLOCK_INVALID`, and `NetworkPeer` fails on it,
tearing down the whole connection (werg/tendriller#103). Not a Tendriller deploy: production deploys were at 11-23 23:41Z and 11-24 12:30Z.
Fixes (commit below): both sessions set `maxClockSkewMs` 10 s (Chronolog's maximum). The page measures and shows its clock skew and
reports it in telemetry. The page always reads the snapshot after connecting or resuming and whenever no read succeeded for a minute.
Before, a page restored from its saved snapshot, or resumed with an unchanged held tick, did not read at all until a new tick arrived.
The stale alert now fires only after a read: "No connection to the DGX" (warn) when a read failed, "Exporter behind" when a read
succeeded but returned old data; a held snapshot shows "refreshing". A skipped owner-replaced reload is retried after the minute
instead of leaving a dead page. Not checked: the page-side runtime (no access to the phone); whether Firefox Android freezes the
SharedWorker in the background; a skew beyond 10 s (it fails the same way).

## 2026-11-24 17:00 The DGX collection yields to round preparation instead of being preempted

- **Observation.** Each aei1 round prepares the next one on the DGX while the Colab A100 trains: `frontier` (4 GB),
  `data` (12 GB, ~1 h), `build` (32 GB, ~15 min), all high. The standing collection (`aei1-collect-vNNNN`, medium,
  budget `kv_gb + 24 + slots x 0.3` = 74 GiB) was preempted for `data` (16:06: 48.9 GiB used, 46.2 available) and
  `build`, and its relaunch needs budget + 15 GiB reserve = 89 GiB free, which the running step and ~40 GB of
  standing claims never leave. It stayed out until the build ended (13:51-14:23 only by a manual claim trim; 16:06-16:19
  until the teacher ended): the GPU idle ~1 h 15 min of a ~2 h round.
- **Cause.** Accounting, then growth. At 16:06 the data step fit physically (46 GiB available - 11 GiB peak leaves
  35 > 15), but the collection's unspent budget reserved half of 25 GiB and other claims ~8: free < 27. The build
  (17.0-17.5 GiB peaks r0004-r0007) comes ~2 h into the collection, when it uses 60-66 GiB: collection + build + 15
  reserve is at the machine's edge, so something must shrink. The collection grows with its age, not round over round
  (claim peaks 41.5-52.5 GiB at ~1 h, 64.8 at 2 h for v0004; restarts reset it). Sampled on v0006 (16:28-16:37, fresh):
  CUDA flat at 19.8 GiB, scheduler/front/collect flat, the 16 shared node collector servers 5.1 -> 6.6 GB in 9 min
  (they recycle only at 1.5 GB RSS each, `cli.ts --recycle-rss-mb`): the growth is in the per-slot part. A full 2 h
  attribution was not measured.
- **Decision: shrink, not stop.** While a round prepares (frontier through build), the driver writes a claim with
  `share` in `ops/ei/held-priority/` (`yield_claim`, heartbeat like a held claim). Every DGX collection then runs
  `PREP_YIELD_SHARE` = 0.5 of its slots (`priority_slots`: the smallest live share; held claims keep 0.75), so its idle
  node servers drain and exit, and lowers its ledger claim to its measured use x 1.1 (`memory_ledger resize yield`;
  `restore` when no claim is left gives back the earlier budget or the guard's raise). Each step first waits until the
  ledger would admit it (`memory_ledger.admissible`, at most `PREP_YIELD_WAIT` = 600 s) and then launches either way,
  so the old preemption is the fallback and prep never waits more than 10 min a step (data fits at once by the numbers
  above; the build comes after an hour of yielding). The build budget goes back to 24 GB (measured 17.5 GiB; the guard
  raises an over-budget unit while memory is plentiful). The 15 GiB reserve is unchanged. Half the slots at full KV
  still decode; a stopped collection decodes nothing.
- **Concurrency and the collection's claim (coordinator, same day).** v0006's engine ran at its cap (`#running-req`
  160 = 128 slots + 32 fill, 5-10 queued, KV 0.61, mamba 0.49, 1.75-1.94k tok/s, ~200-270 own episodes/h); decode is
  bandwidth-bound and KV has room: `DGX_COLLECT_SLOTS` = 192 (224 running with the fill), opt-out `--slots 128`. Its
  claim is now measured, one function for every DGX collection site (`dgx_collection_budget_gb`: async standing,
  cycle collect, halt recollect): engine kv + 20 (v0006: CUDA 19.8 + host 10.7 GiB at 12 GB KV) + 0.2 GiB per slot
  (per-slot part ~0.07 fresh, ~0.14 at 1 h, ~0.27 at 2 h): 70 GiB at 192 slots (58 at 128) instead of
  kv + 24 + 0.3/slot (94 at 192: unreadmittable, and 74 at 128). Past it the guard raises the claim while memory is
  plentiful. Expected at 192: ~83 GiB at 2 h at the 2 h rate; yielding to prep (96 slots) ~57, leaving ~20 GiB over the
  build's 17.5 beside it. Risk: if the per-slot part keeps growing at 192 the floor guard (available < 20) may stop
  the collection late in a round; watch `aei1-collect-v*` peaks after the restart. The throughput change is read from
  `actor.log` after the next restart.
- **Rejected.** Smaller collection all the time (costs throughput in the other ~45 min); prep at medium priority (waits
  without bound behind the collection, on the critical path: r0007's SFT waited 14 min for its prep); a lower node
  recycle threshold (shared collector mechanism of GRPO and held too; not needed once the prep steps fit).
- **Inventory** (sizes, starts, requeues or preempts the DGX collection or a prep step):
  `expert_iteration.py`: `COLLECTOR_SLOT_GB`/`REMOTE_COLLECTOR_SLOT_GB`, `STAGE_PRIORITY`/`COLLECTION_PRIORITY`,
  `priority_slots`/`held_priority_claims` and `FrontierCollector._priority` (the in-place shrink, now also the ledger
  resize), `collect` (actor KV and running cap, `--unit-prefix` = ledger unit), `Cycle.ledger`/`present`/`wait`,
  `Cycle.collect_stage`, `halt` recollect, `_fill_window` actor, cycle `frontier_stage`/`data_stage`/`build_stage`
  (now under the same yield: a speculative next cycle's collection may run beside them), `rebuild` (32 GB, left: it
  runs only on a rebuild request), `AsyncRoundDriver.ensure_collection`, `remote_collect_argv`/`start_remote_collector`
  (remote collectors hold no engine and are not shrunk: `priority_dir=None` for `--actor`), `prepare` (changed),
  `train_sft` (stops the collection for a DGX SFT: unchanged, the learner needs the memory), `recap`/GRPO/`publish`
  (high stages at a round's end, when the collection is replaced anyway: unchanged), `dgx_held` (claims held priority:
  unchanged, now also lowers the claim). `memory_ledger.py`: `outstanding`, `headroom`, `preemption_plan`,
  `requeue_spec`, `plan_launch`, `default_reserve`, `learned_budget`/`family`, guard budget raise and `victim`
  (unchanged; `resize`, `yield_claim`, `restore_claim`, `admissible` added). grpo's own collector (GRPO rounds) does
  not read the claims: a GRPO round is itself a high stage and stops the collection.
- **Rollout.** Opt-out `--prep-yield-share 1` (async-drive and cycle; or `NATLANG_EI_PREP_YIELD_SHARE=1`). The running
  driver takes it at its next restart on a new pin; a collection still running from the old pin reads the claim as a
  held claim (0.75 of its slots, no ledger resize), so each step falls back to the preemption after its 10 min wait.
  Tests: `test_a_yielding_collection_lowers_its_claim_so_a_waiting_stage_fits_beside_it_and_restores_it`
  (test_memory_ledger.py), `test_round_preparation_claim_shrinks_the_dgx_collection_further_and_its_ledger_claim_follows`
  (test_colab_and_profiles.py), `test_round_preparation_runs_beside_a_yielding_collection_instead_of_preempting_it` and
  `test_wait_for_room_is_bounded_and_skipped_when_opted_out` (test_async_train.py). Telemetry: `held priority` and
  `ledger claim` events in the collection's `collect.log`, `prep yield` notes in `drive.log`, `claim yield`/`claim
  restore` ledger events.

## 2026-11-24 18:00 A DGX collection launched during round preparation starts shrunk; preparation lets it in first

- **Observation (coordinator, pin-1a8157454419).** At the r0007 publish (17:18) `aei1-collect-v0007` (192 slots,
  70 GB) launched while `aei1-r0008-build` (old driver, 32 GB) ran: it waited with need 85 vs 82.4 obtainable, GPU at
  0% for 11 min, until the build was adopted down to 24 GB. The yield lowered a claim only once a collection ran; a
  collection launched under a live prep claim asked for its full size although its collector starts at the share.
- **Fix.** `Cycle.collection_budget(slots)`: with a live round-preparation claim (`prep_share`: the smallest `share`
  of the claims; held claims carry none) a DGX collection launches at `dgx_collection_budget_gb(kv, slots x share)`
  (51 GB at 192 x 0.5) and passes its full size (`collect --ledger-full-gb`, 70); when the claim ends the collector
  restores to it (`memory_ledger resize restore --budget-gb`: the largest of the current, pre-yield and full budget).
  Every DGX launch site uses it (async `ensure_collection`, cycle `collect_stage`, `halt` recollect). The driver's own
  collection goes first: `Cycle.wait_for_room` also waits while `AsyncRoundDriver.collection_pending()` (its newest
  policy's collection queued in the ledger, not running), within the same 10 min bound, so a prep step queued at high
  priority never holds the relaunch after a publish out. A step already admitted is not touched; the shrunk launch
  is what lets the collection in beside it. Opt-out unchanged (`--prep-yield-share 1` launches at full size).
- **Test.** `test_a_collection_launched_during_round_preparation_starts_shrunk_and_preparation_lets_it_in_first`
  (test_async_train.py), restore-to-full cases in test_memory_ledger.py and test_colab_and_profiles.py.

1. **Repetition across rounds.** Each round re-trained the fixed teacher pool from the previous round's policy: kept
   filled-reasoning episodes trained before 78% (r2), 83% (r3), 91% (r4), 98% (r5), 96% (r7); teacher 7% (r2) to 93%
   (r5). Admitted episodes with 5-7 earlier exposures: 1,372 by round 8. `prefer-unseen` only puts unseen first; the
   round size then fills with repeats, and which repeats is arbitrary (one subset every round).
2. **Own share from old policies.** The per-task cap in `student_selection` picked own producers at random, so the
   step-4 priority's frontier-policy preference (async-train §3) never applied under it. Round 7 kept 834 own
   episodes: 383 from aei1 collections (43 from v0005, the trained policy's), 451 from grpo-v3/v4/v5 and sft-v7..v9
   collections, which carry 55% of the own target tokens.

**Fixes (default on, opt-outs, targeted tests).**
- `held_eval`: `compare` (CLI) relabels a result written before `infra_lost` from its directory (`load_result`;
  `--no-relabel`, `NATLANG_HELD_RELABEL=0`); `ran_out_rate` leaves lost episodes out of its denominator;
  `ran_out_rate_delta` is the change over the matched pairs the primary uses (`ran_out_rate_delta_unpaired` kept;
  `NATLANG_HELD_RAN_OUT_DELTA=unpaired` restores both). Consumers: the driver's `judge`/`verdict_stage` (through the
  compare CLI), the dashboard (reads `ran_out_rate` as recorded; left out: it does not import held_eval and a
  relabelled result is not written back, so round 1's dashboard row keeps 0.0742).
- `sft_sources build`: no repetition, **the owner's decision for the current aei1 rounds (2026-11-24: "I don't want
  to train on repetition at all"; not a standing rule)**: `--max-prior-exposures 1` (default; 0: off, the old rule;
  N: an episode may train N times) drops every core episode (teacher, October, rl-own, jolt-guided) and every aux unit
  (filled, operators, neuralese-graph, own-neuralese-graph, fallow22, live) that any `--prefer-unseen` build trained:
  candidates before admission, aux units in `take_unit`, and all chains again before the round cap (reported in
  `target_cap.exposure_cap` and the funnel's `over_exposed`). Trained units go least-trained first at the round cap
  and in share-bounded aux parts (`Exposures`, also in `recap`), which matters only with the opt-out. A round with
  little unseen data is smaller, never padded; a mix whose live goals all trained before skips the open-goal
  distinctness check instead of failing. Round 8's mix under the rule would have kept ~1,270 of its ~9,170 episodes
  (teacher 385 of 3,295, filled 232 of 5,005, own 655 of 867).
  - Lineage: aei1's `prefer_unseen` holds sft-v7..v9 and r0001..r0007 but not `runs/sft-mix-20261120-v2`, sft-v6's
    data (sft-v6 started from the base 5ff07638; sft-v7 from sft-v6): it belongs in the lineage. The GRPO runs
    (grpo-v3..v6) are no ancestors (they trained from the base, not into this lineage); their episodes are repeats

- `sft_sources build`: `--own-cap-order recent` (default; `any`: old rule) ranks the frontier policy's and its
  previous policy's own successes before older policies' under the per-task, family and wrapper caps.

## 2026-11-24 20:40 Program-tuning fits: the norm adjoint's per-block loop removed (0f16e04fa), exact, ~1.9x per step

**Bottleneck.** Program-tuning fits train adapters only, so every `Lfm3RMSNorm` gain is frozen
(`requires_grad=False`, BF16). `_RowwiseNormAdjoint.backward` sent frozen gains to its per-128-row Python replay
(one norm forward plus one `autograd.grad` per 128-row block). The q/k norms have tokens x heads rows, so that is
thousands of iterations per call. The batched exact adjoint (`_batched/_windowed_lfm3_norm_adjoint`) required a
trainable gain. A DGX repro (`ext_decisions_tree` plan, fresh fit, 4 steps; ledger units `progtune-prof-ab2`, the
backward timed per call) put 86.5 s of norm backward in those 4 steps: 47.4 s for q/k norms (width 128, 704 calls)
and 37.6 s for hidden norms (width 2048, 1,330 calls).

**Fix (0f16e04fa, default on, `NATLANG_NORM_BATCHED_FROZEN=0` opts out).** Frozen gains take the batched and windowed
adjoint too. It returns dx only and builds no per-block gain parts. Inventory: `_RowwiseNormAdjoint` is installed by
`configure_norm_execution` (`native_composite.py:329`, `shared_state.py:1008`) on every native LFM3 port. Its
consumers are every native-graph gradient path: `tune.build`/`JointTrainer` (program tuning, distill, families,
learned), `serve/native_grad.py` (whole-graph Neuralese gradients, operator soft states) and `tune/rl.py`. The fix
lives in the one shared function, so it reaches all of them. Not applicable: the GRPO/SFT learner
(`train/lfm3_fast.py:134` `_rms`, its own compiled norm; it does not use the native port).

**Exactness.** Norm tests (37, CUDA included, under the ledger): the frozen-gain batched adjoint is bit-identical to
the per-block loop and to the concatenated forward's adjoint at 129-16,401 rows and widths 64/2048. End to end, the
4-step A/B fits from one seed have identical per-step row losses. Their adapter and optimizer artifacts after step 4
are byte-identical (content-addressed artifact ids and `state.json` equal). In-flight fits therefore resume on the
new code without any change in their numbers.

**Speed** (DGX, GPU shared with the aei1 collection, so absolute times are noisy). Steps 2-4: 169.8/115.3/87.8 s
before and 102.4/61.5/36.1 s after, 373 s -> 200 s (1.86x; 0.48 -> 0.90 steps/min). Norm backward: 86.5 s -> 3.0 s
over 4 steps. On the L4 (2.5 min/step, 37% of it in this loop by py-spy) the expected step is ~1.6 min. Not measured
on Colab.

**Switch-over.** The fits run `tune.build` on the VM at `--commit` (`l4-fits2.sh` and `l4-seq.sh`:
`COMMIT=de2b36add`; `colab-seq*.sh` take it as an argument). A lane picks the fix up when it is relaunched with a
commit containing 0f16e04fa. The pin for the driver scripts needs no change: the fix is VM-side code. Resuming from
state.json is exact (above).

**Not checked.** Step timing on the L4/A100 itself. FP32-gain profiles (`fp32-norms-v1`): their gains keep the
per-block loop, because the fast path still requires BF16 gains and program tuning does not use FP32 gains. The
trainable-gain path's per-block Python sum of gain parts (`_sum_norm_gain_parts`, kept for exact BF16 fan-in
order). The small-input forward's per-128-row loop (`rowwise_norm_forward` below 4,096 rows). What dominates the
remaining ~60 s/step: py-spy is not permitted on the DGX, and a cProfile run (`progtune-prof-cp1`) was queued
behind the collection.

## 2026-11-24 21:40 SGLang adapter slots: the adapted decode graph read a freed attention plan (CUDA illegal memory access); fixed in fork 7a29eff9ee (adapter-serving strand)

**Observations.** The route adapter arm (Colab L4, one slot, every request adapted) died at its first batch of 27
running with a CUDA illegal memory access, reported in xgrammar's bitmask kernel (a sticky error). T3 (05:10) had
recorded the same fault at 4 running. The base arm runs with `--sglang-adapter-slots 0` and never faulted.

**Inventory.** The mechanism is a per-request adapter stack applied at serving. Below are every engine and consumer of
it, and where the defect lives: decode CUDA graphs captured per variant.

| Component | Role | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python native engine (`native_adapters.run_native`, `engine.py` `_native_run`) | reference, eager | reference; captures no graph variants |
| SGLang actor + fork (`sglang_actor._sglang_adapter_file` / `_adapter_acquire` / `adapter_cache_key`; fork `lfm3.py` `NatlangAdapters`, `decode_cuda_graph_runner` lora/nolora capture, `flashinfer_backend._prepare_cuda_graph_metadata`) | slots | defect found and fixed (below); scores not yet re-measured |
| Managed llama-server (fork `build_lora_mm`, ts-host `llama/server.ts` `--lora-per-sequence`, `model/lora-scales.ts`) | GGUF LoRA, per-request scales | T3: 288/288 serial (`-np 1`); shared batches (`-np 4`) not run (harness `--parallel` added) |
| In-page wllama (vendored natlang-b12092) | same fork code, wasm CPU | T3: 144/144; no device graphs |
| Upstream SGLang LoRA (`triton_v2` `skip_inactive_dense_lora`) | the same dual capture | fixed by the same backend change (shared code) |
| Other attention backends' per-bs capture metadata | trtllm_mla decode reused like its verify tiers (fixed); hpc_ops and xpu build metadata as views of shared buffers (no orphan); flashinfer_mla (`flashinfer_mla_backend.py:376-397`) still builds a wrapper per capture | left out: no model the fork serves uses MLA, and its plan patching (`fast_mla_decode_plan` installed after the first `begin_forward`) needs its own reuse path that no available model can test |
| serve_native_checkpoint (slot rank, slots per actor), pop_rl_actor `serve_colab_tenant_actor` (1 slot for adapter arms), pop_actor_driver `adapter_args` | launch | new gate: no slots on a fork without the fix |
| program_tune (`colab-measure --arm adapter`, merged arm becad4efb), LoRA mixtures (`tune/learned`: composed stacks on the same slot path), held_eval (`policy_id_of`: identity only), ts-host `neuralese-server.ts` / `rollout-episodes.mjs` / `s7_decode_probe.py` (wire only) | consumers | no adapter result measured on slots exists to invalidate (route `adapter-dev64-l4` scored 0) |

**Root cause.** The fork captures each decode batch size twice when adapter slots exist: "lora" first, then
"nolora" (`_lora_backend_skips_inactive`). FlashInfer's `_prepare_cuda_graph_metadata` created new decode wrappers
for every capture and overwrote `decode_cuda_graph_metadata[bs]`. The "lora" graph therefore baked in the first
wrapper set's buffers: the int workspace holding the plan, and qo_indptr. A replay plans only the stored set. Every
adapted decode step thus ran kernels over a plan that no replay writes, from wrappers that were garbage-collected
after capture. Where that memory was unmapped or reused, the result was an illegal memory access. Where it stayed
mapped, attention ran on a stale capture-time plan.

This predicts the observations. Base-only batches replay the correctly planned "nolora" graph, so the base arm (0
slots) and all collection are unaffected. Adapted serving faults or drifts in decode only. Whether it faults depends
on where the freed buffers land: it faulted on the L4 at 27 running and in T3 at 4 running, while a GB10 run at 2
running completed. T3's pre-fix adapted turns sat 2.6 nats from native (top-1 0.34), and this defect predicts wrong
adapted decode on top of the prefix-cache defect fixed there. A static investigator found the mechanism and
independently cited the code: `flashinfer_backend.py:765`, `:1328-1332`; `decode.py` workspace and qo_indptr
allocation; replay planning at `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1881`.

**Reproduction (GB10, ledger units of 15-20 GB).** On 17e3458c2e, with 32 running, BF16 KV, 8192-token chunks and
mixed requests, the run did not fault. With 64 running, FP8 KV and 4096-token chunks (the L4 tenant's settings), all
adapted, it faulted at the first decode after the prefills (`adslot-repro-6`). On 7a29eff9ee, with the same settings
and adapted and base requests at once, it served 192 requests at up to 64 running with 0 native fallbacks and no fault
(`adslot-fix-3`). The captures are in `/mnt/external/adapter-slots-20261124/runs/f3-l4like/captures.json`.

**Fix (defaults, opt-outs, tests).**
- Fork 7a29eff9ee (doc 6c4a42b624, branch natlang). The graphs of one batch size share its FlashInfer decode, verify
  and draft-extend wrappers; they are rebuilt only when the token width or verify kind changes. TRT-LLM MLA decode
  metadata is reused the way its verify tiers already were. Opt-out: `NATLANG_SHARE_GRAPH_WRAPPERS=0`. Marker:
  `NATLANG_SHARED_GRAPH_WRAPPERS`. CPU tests: `test/natlang/test_graph_variant_wrappers.py` (4 passed).
- natlang 63a71cd9d: `serve_native_checkpoint.adapter_slots_on_fork` serves 0 slots on a fork without the marker, so
  adapted turns run on the native engine. Opt-out: `NATLANG_SGLANG_ADAPTER_SLOTS_ANY_FORK=1`. Test added in
  `test_sglang_source_attestation.py`. `sglang-fork.json` now points to the fork head. Harnesses gained
  `check_sglang_adapter_parity.py --concurrency/--adapted-only/--server-arg/--merged` and
  `check_tuned_lora_llama_parity.py --parallel N`.
- **Rollout.** The DGX checkout `/home/werg/sglang-natlang`, which live actors import and Colab bootstraps from, stays
  at 17e3458c2e. Moving it changes the attested engine, and held pairs stay within one fork commit, so it moves at the
  next experiment boundary. Until then, adapter arms on Colab run their adapted turns on the native engine (the gate),
  and the merged arm (becad4efb) stays the way program tuning serves fits.

**Not done / not checked.**
- Scores and greedy tokens on 7a29eff9ee against the native stack and against the merged checkpoint (8ceb7cd8) have
  not been measured. The reference runs were stopped after a few minutes, at the coordinator's request, to readmit the
  aei1 collection. They need Pop idle (it was serving aei1's held actor) or a ~20 GB DGX slot: `repro.sh f3-l4like ''
  64 64 48 --phase reference` and `--merged`.
- llama-server with adapted and base sequences in one batch (`--parallel 4`) has not run (CPU, 22 GB peak).
- Not checked: ggml CUDA graphs on a GPU llama-server; flashinfer_mla (left out, above); the held-task outcome of an
  adapter served on slots; Colab L4/A100 runs of the fix (only the GB10 was run).

Owner: "take subagent-heavy existing agentic training data and just turn the subagent to parent connections into
neuralese to train that in". Refined the same day: no conversion to natlang programs. The data is a source of format
and domain diversity that still trains Neuralese. Design and results: `plans/neuralese/SUBAGENT_NEURALESE_20261124.md`.
Code: `scripts/neuralese_data/subagent_neuralese.py` (acb78d91e, e35ad7411, c78a1e37b, ea505717b).

- **Mapping.**
  - Each lead and subagent conversation stays as recorded and is rendered by the engine's chat template for the
    student. SearchSwarm's in-prompt Qwen tool block becomes structured tools in the student's call format.
  - Each report the lead receives becomes a Neuralese value written from the report's text. In the default
    `--read-mode splice` this is the learner's existing pass-through: consume markers, placeholder rows and an import
    in the lead's prompt, with the producer document `[produce_open] + written ids`. The lead's later replies train the
    producer computation and the marker rows.
  - Every recorded reply is a target. Teacher reasoning, lead-in text, prompts, tool outputs and the spans are zero
    weight.
- **Recorded tool outputs are zero-weight context, and the October "not replayable" exclusion does not apply.** That
  rule excluded October rows because they predated the answer protocol and would have taught a retired natlang
  surface (2026-11-18). These rows claim no natlang surface: they are other harnesses' conversations kept in their
  own format, and the student never sees them as natlang calls. Their outputs are what the teacher actually saw, so
  the teacher's next action is conditioned on the true observation. Admission instead rests on the source's own
  verification: WideSeek `item_f1` (depth 1.0, width >= 0.9), and SearchSwarm's gold answer contained in the lead's
  final answer.

  context-free write read back 0/12. Only the spliced read trains the Neuralese operators, which is the owner's goal
  for this data. `--read-mode inline` builds the serving-identical variant, which is plain text and trains no
  operator.

(root stem abstracted from the paths), its frontmatter types with literal unions collapsed, its text with digits,

cover 425 shapes (307 effective), the top two (reasoning-gym arc-1d and rectangle-count wrappers) 50 groups each.

**Change.** `grpo.cap_shapes` reorders a collection order so that no shape takes more than `SHAPE_CAP` (0.01) of any
prefix beyond its first 4 rows; a capped row waits and enters as soon as the prefix has grown; nothing is dropped
(only capped shapes left: least-placed first). It applies after the tiers and the family round-robin, so it overrides

`explore-constructs.json` records it). Driver opt-out: `--select-args "--shape-cap 0"`.

## 2026-11-25 Neuralese states are written in their producing context; the context-free text write is gone (neuralese-write strand)

Owner, 2026-11-25: "The whole idea with Neuralese is to write it out in such a way that it attends to the text that
precedes it, but then that preceding text, of course, doesn't propagate to wherever the Neuralese embeddings get used.
… the compression function is you take some sort of text and have it return a model-generated summary, and the span
of the summary is where the Neuralese handover happens." About the text write: "That context-free write, if I
understand it correctly, sounds like a massive bug."

**Inventory: where a state is created from text, and whether its producing context was there.**

| Component | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Python native engine `native_write_text` (`serve/engine.py`) | context-free: `[produce_open] + text` from position 0 | the span after its producing call (`write_context`, `capture_plan(text=)`) |
| SGLang actor `_sglang_write_text` | context-free | the same plan, one fork capture request |
| Managed llama-server | no text writer (typed `Neuralese<T>` from text failed) | `grammarWritePort`: `grammarCapture` in write mode |
| In-page wllama | no text writer, no capture | unchanged: gap row in ENGINE_PARITY with its blocker |
| `native.capture` / grammar capture (operators, compact_history) | in context (the reply in its own call) | unchanged |
| `native.init-body` (soft states, guidance primed in the call) | in context (its real position in the call) | unchanged; its placeholder is now an in-context write |
| Produce spans sampled in generation (template write readout) | in context | unchanged |
| ts-host typed result / typed JSON result / result field (`runtime.ts writeNeuraleseText`) | `port.write(text)`, no context | the call's latest turn (`noteProducingCall`, `callContext`: exact prompt and reply ids from the RL capture, else messages and tools) |
| ts-host literals `<|neuralese|>…` (`decodeNeuralese` → `writeLiterals`) | no context | the turn that wrote them |
| ts-host typed argument (`materializeSoftStringArguments`) | no context | the caller's latest turn; none for an outside input |
| writeGuidance / writeHint (`training-guidance.ts`) | no context | the writer call's turn |
| Guidance with `guidancePriming: 'text'`, library values (`combinators.ts`), text-init placeholders, memetic guidance (`memetic_workspace.py`), `tune/soft.py`, `tune/learned/growth.py` | context-free | no producing call: the engine's producer call (`text_producer_messages`: the text as the user's message, the span as the answer) |
| Learner pass-through (`lower_rollout_turns.write_sources`, `exp0_sft`, `grpo`, `lfm3_fast.passthrough_plan`) | computed whatever document was recorded | unchanged code path: new rollouts record the in-context document; SFT (`sft_sources neuralese-graph`) rewrites legacy context-free typed-result writes to the span after their producing turn (`write_sources(in_context=…)`, opt-out `--recorded-write-documents`); GRPO keeps the recorded document (exact replay) |
| Whole-graph replay (`rl/native_replay.py`) | refused any writer document but the standalone one | accepts a token document with context; still refuses a producing prompt that imported a spliced state |
| `subagent_neuralese.py` (D01, D02) | `[produce_open] + report` | the report at the end of the subagent's own call (below) |
| `operator_ablation.py` `standalone` arm | context-free on purpose (an ablation) | unchanged |
| Read side: `in-context-text` bypass (`engine.reads_in_context`, fork `native_state_registry::resolve`) | text writes and spans read as tokens | unchanged default (see the probe); legacy `text` kind keeps its own opt-out |

**Decision: what produces a plain text value with no producing call.** A call that receives the value and writes it
back as its answer: the text as the user's message, then the span after the generation prompt (an empty thought
closed). The span attends to the value and to a real call frame (BOS, turn markers). The engine owns this frame, so
every caller of `write-text` without a context (memetic guidance, library values, placeholders) gets it from one
place. A sampled model-generated summary was not chosen: a `Neuralese<string>` value must hold its text exactly, and
the learned compaction operators (`view`, `compact_history`) are the summary path and already capture in context.

**Fix.** `native.text-write` takes the producing call (`prompt_token_ids` | `prompt_segments`, `reply_token_ids`, or
`messages`/`tools`; `/v1/neuralese/info` lists `native.text-write.context`); the state is
`prompt + reply up to its end of turn (+ </think> if open) + produce_open + text`, header `producer_kind: "span"`.
The consumer still receives only the span's rows.
A producing context that no longer fits the model's context with the text falls back to the producer call above
(`Engine.write_in_context`). An empty text writes an empty state, as before.

**Read side: the in-context-text bypass stays the default.** Probe (`neuralese_readback_probe.py`, the aei1 r0001
policy `8e634a0f`, native engine BF16 on the DGX, `NATLANG_NEURALESE_SPAN_IN_CONTEXT=0 NATLANG_NEURALESE_TEXT_IN_CONTEXT=0`
so every state is spliced, 24 synthetic texts, greedy, the runtime's `natlang.read` prompt, exact `return_result`):

| Arm | Read back | Receipt |
|---|---|---|
| state: write-text with no producing call (the engine's producer call) | 0/24 | exact-native-state 24 |
| context: write-text after a producer call's messages | 0/24 | exact-native-state 24 |
| captured: the text captured in place in a producer reply (`select`) | 0/24 | exact-native-state 24 |
| inline: the text in the reader's own prompt | 19/24 | none |
| shuffled: another text's state | 0/24 | exact-native-state 24 |

Every spliced reply was the same text-independent opening ("We need to understand the task. The user says: …"):
the policy ignores a spliced state, wherever it was written. Writing in context is the precondition for a readable
handover, not sufficient for an untrained reader; the rebuilt subagent data (below) trains spliced reads of
in-context states through the learner pass-through. Until the probe passes spliced on a trained policy, engines keep
reading text writes and spans as their tokens (`NATLANG_NEURALESE_SPAN_IN_CONTEXT`, default on), so serving
behaviour does not change. Flipping the default is an OPEN_ITEMS row.

**Also fixed on the way** (test failures seen in this work): `test_native_typed_harness` counted split-tokenization
alternative nodes (716a9d0fc) as invocations and compared raw option scores with the logsumexp readout; the recorded
objective's prompt check refused a decision capture whose prompt holds the options' shared prefix
(`native_learning._shared_into_prompt`). Its error now names the first differing item.

## 2026-11-25 03:10 Program tuning: ext_decisions_verdict's merged arm 0/128 was a fit on empty-reply rows (fixed everywhere; five fits invalid)

**Observation.** `progtune-l4-seq-3`, 02:42: ext_decisions_verdict merged vs base on dev64 (l4 series, de2b36add)
0.0 vs 0.7266 (0/128 vs 93/128). Every merged episode ended `model_incomplete: terminated_without_result (repeated
immediate EOS after one recovery turn)`: 0-1 completion tokens per call ("up", then EOS), 47 s for 128 episodes.

**Cause.** The fit's `rows.jsonl` held 16 turns (of 1,280) whose reply had neither text nor a tool call (teacher turns
of pool-progtune-decisions t000069/t000089 and pool-v2-rich t004625/t006207/t017043 that the runtime answered with a
recovery turn). `program_tune.episode_turns` admitted them (no tool call, so no rejected or unverified event), and
`tune.rows.turn_graph` lowered each to one weighted token, `<|im_end|>` (a teacher reply's think block is context).
`tune.objective.program_loss` averages per row, so each such row weighed as much as a whole reply: the fit's row losses
show them at 7.3-11.4 nats (steps 2, 13, 21, 30, 46). Evidence that the weights, not serving, ended the replies: HF
forward on the DGX (independent of SGLang and the Colab export): P(`<|im_end|>`) at the first generated position 0.75-0.84
on verdict and route prompts with the merged verdict checkpoint, e^-19..-22 with the base, e^-11 with the route merged
checkpoint (route's rows: 0 empty replies, merged arm 0.8438 vs 0.8828). The prompts were identical (5,081 prompt tokens
on both arms' first call), the actor attested 95df57f2 with the same export format and config as route's arm, and the
episodes were scored as model failures (no infra losses, no timeouts). The release's factors were finite and of the
usual size (per-family LoRA delta norms within 1.3x of route's).

**Fix (default, opt-out `NATLANG_TUNE_EMPTY_REPLIES=train` / `--empty-replies train`).** One predicate
(`tune.rows.empty_reply`, `empty_reply_message`): a reply with no visible text and no tool call (a decision turn never
is) is no positive target. Where the mechanism lives:
- `program_tune.episode_turns` (tune-turn producer): disposition `empty-reply`, counted in `rows.json`
  `empty_reply_turns`.
- `tune.rows.lower_rows` (every tune-turn consumer: program fits, the bank's `program_rows`, ts-host `tune
  collect`/`pool`/`distill` rows, memetic and operator soft-state rows): drops them, so rows files written before the fix
  are safe too.
- `sft_sources build` (expert-iteration mixes: r0007 1,283 and r0008 1,382 such teacher rows of ~125k) and `sft_sources
  neuralese-graph` (own calls): dropped, counted as `empty_reply_calls`.
- Left out: GRPO (`lower_rollout_turns.episode_turns`, `grpo.py`): on-policy, an empty sampled reply trains with its
  group advantage (negative in a failed episode), which is the signal RL wants, not a positive target.

**Results invalidated and rerun.** Rows of five programs held empty replies: verdict 16/1,280, bgkit_pubmed_reading
45/5,301, bgkit_searchqa_reading 336/12,568, composed_multihop_deep 173/11,718, composed_neuralese_iterate 247/7,146
(route, tally, tree, apigen retail: 0). Their rows were repaired in place (the old file, fits and arms under
`DIR/fit/invalid-empty-reply-20261125-025649/` with `INVALID.json`): verdict's release and merged arm (the 0/128),
searchqa's A100 release (not yet measured), and the in-progress pubmed (step 40) and neuralese_iterate (step 11) fits,
which I stopped with their lanes `progtune-l4-fits3-a/b` (they were producing invalid releases). No other measured arm
was affected (route merged -3.9 pts and its adapter arms trained on 0 empty rows). The fits restart from scratch on the
repaired rows at the same tenant commit 206b5ebd6 (`progtune-l4-fits4-a/b`: verdict, pubmed, neuralese_iterate,
multihop, searchqa); `progtune-l4-seq-readd` relaunches the measurement lane as `progtune-l4-seq-4` with verdict back in
its list once its new release is home and l4-seq-3 is idle. The bank stage (after l4-seq) lowers rows with the pinned
pin-51cf1173c code, which predates the `lower_rows` guard, but it reads the repaired rows files.

### 2026-11-25 — account for resolver-prefixed provider DNS failures

The actual V27 wave0055 failure `natlang ...: failed: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN
chatgpt.com` was missed by the transport classifier, which recognized the DNS
code only without its resolver prefix. That spent a goal attempt on a provider
failure. Recognize resolver-prefixed transient DNS codes within the existing
failed-call envelope; circuit-breaker/HTTP wrappers remain supported. Descriptions
of a DNS failure inside document text or schema errors still do not classify as
transport. Three generic `terminated` records remain under investigation rather
than being blanket-reclassified. All original packets and receipts stay intact;
status recomputes their accounting under the repaired driver at resume. Actual
53 campaign tests passed; collection's existing accounting opt-out still applies.

## 2026-11-25 05:45 Pop actor OOM: init-body reloaded the native model into the CPU front; init-body runs on SGLang, Pop's held-serve MemoryMax is the 10.5 GB cap

- **Observations.** aei1's Pop actor (`popheld-8e634a0f46ce-*`, SGLang on Pop's host, MemoryMax 9.5 GiB) was
  OOM-killed at 04:48 and 05:17 after 27-60 min of serving. The kernel reports name the front
  (`serve_native_checkpoint.py --device cpu`) as the victim both times with 5.7-5.8 GB anon (it starts at 0.86 GB);
  cgroup anon was 9.9 GB, file cache 0.24 GB. The actor log shows the native model's `Loading weights 287/287` in
  the middle of serving 12 and 15 min before each kill (04:36:18, 05:02:45), not at startup; the faulting thread was
  in a scalar float loop (a CPU forward).
- **Cause.** `SglangEngine.native_init_body` (the `native-states/init-body` endpoint: a Neuralese body initialized
  from its text at its rendered position, `ts-host/src/neuralese/text-init.ts`) had no SGLang path: every call ran the
  native engine, whose first use lazily reloads the released native model (`_ensure_native`) into the front. On
  Pop the front is a CPU process: the 3.46 GB BF16 view plus CPU forwards of the call took it to ~5.8 GB beside the
  scheduler's 2.4 GB and the 9.5 GB cap killed the unit, and with it 64 collection slots. The DGX actor of the same
  collection shows the same route: `init_body` is its only native endpoint (12 calls, ~104 s each), and its native
  model is resident. Write-text and capture already ran on SGLang (`write_text_sglang`, 2026-11-12).
- **Fix (default on).** `native_init_body` runs on SGLang (`_sglang_init_body`): the shared `Engine.init_body_plan`
  renders the call, imports before the body go through `_sglang_import` as in generation, and one capture request
  through the body stores the block (the tokens after the body are recorded in the source capture but not computed:
  they cannot change the body's causal state). Same result fields as the native path (`init_body_result`). Adapted
  calls and a front with no SGLang keep the native path; `NATLANG_SGLANG_INIT_BODY=0` opts out. Metric
  `natlang_native_endpoint_*{endpoint="init_body_sglang"}`. Every SGLang front (DGX, Colab, Pop) takes it.
  Found on the way: `Engine.prompt_positions` (every init-body, and any caller that sizes a prompt with imports) asked
  `_native_exact`, which reads the native backbone's layer kinds and so reloaded the model by itself.
  `SglangEngine._native_exact` answers from the export (`_sglang_exact`, the same identity and layer-kind check) while
  the model is released.
- **Cap.** `_serve_pop` (held serve and the aei1 Pop actor) passed only `--budget-gb 9.5`, so MemoryMax was the claim,
  not the `SGLANG_MEMORY_GB - 0.5` = 10.5 GB that `start` already set; its comment said the engine ran in a docker
  container capped by `--memory`, which is true only for the native engine. Both paths now take
  `pop_sglang_ledger_args()` (claim 9.5, MemoryMax 10.5).
- **Enters:** the Pop actor at its next serve from a pin with this commit (the aei1 driver re-serves Pop after an
  exit); the DGX and Colab fronts at their next serve. A front already serving keeps the native route until then.
- **Tests:** `test_sglang_actor.py::test_init_body_runs_on_sglang_and_matches_the_native_engine` (an imported state
  before the body, text after it: same init/source-capture fields and block tensors as the native engine, native
  model stays released), `test_pop_held_detached.py::test_start_and_serve_checkpoint_claim_one_admissible_pop_budget`.
- **Not checked:** other native-only endpoints on an SGLang front (adapted write/capture/turns, and the native
  endpoints `encode`, `embed`, gradients and optimizers) still reload the native model; on Pop's CPU front any of
  them can do the same. No guard refuses a reload that cannot fit the unit's cap. The live Pop actor was not
  watched through an init-body call after the fix (it serves the old code until its next serve).

## 2026-11-25 10:10 Invented programs: quality at the top of the funnel; reviews only on a drawn sample (program-inventor agent)

**Owner (2026-11-25):** "our qualification and admittance process is too heavy ... we need to create masses of data. So
it's fine if individual samples are not perfect ... optimize how we generate ... so that at the top of the funnel, we
start generating high quality stuff on average." "I think reviews should only be on a drawn sample."

**Why.** Wave 1 (8 Sonnet builds, about 25 review rounds) spent most of its inference on review-fix loops, and the
same seven failures recurred across rounds: text stating its judgment's answer, arithmetic and comparison inside
judgments, scripted answers following a rule written nowhere (or only in NOTES) or applied unevenly, items with two
readings where rules overlap or a definition has no direction, types that cannot hold what the text says, hand-derived
expected answers wrong by the code's order, and fixes by deleting the trap. Each is cheaper to prevent in the brief and
a builder self-check than to find in review.

**Process change.**
- Qualification admits (1a884f706). A review is one sampled pass (`invented.py sample-reviews N`; `REVIEW_BRIEF.md`):
  grades, `wrong_expected` (only answers a careful reader rejects), and up to five `funnel_findings` for the brief and
  skill. No requests to the builder, no rounds. `invented.py publish` withholds a program whose review of the admitted
  version lists `wrong_expected`. The program-inventor app's per-program judged gate (`meetsBar.nl`) is removed for the
  same reason (DECOMPOSITION part 10).
- `BUILD_BRIEF.md`: a "One answer per item" section teaches the seven failures as positive habits with short worked
  examples, and a self-check runs before qualify (`<slug>.SELFCHECK.md`: re-answer every scripted item from the
  instruction and types without NOTES; every text a judgment sees against its answer; every number, date and
  comparison with the TypeScript line doing it). Review rounds and the "expect two or three rounds" loop are gone;
  ledger commands use medium priority, `--no-resumable`, `--wait-exit`. Skill: patterns.md (overlaps and directions,
  leave the answer to the judgment, types hold what the text says), SKILL.md step 3 (quantities read, code computes),
  language/refinements facts builders hit (`Date`, exported signature types, `untrusted(...)` through `decide`).
- Tooling (c5f116d44): `invented.py dry-run [--controls]` (no model; 35 s with every control on a wave-1 submission,
  against 5-40 min for qualify), qualify never leaves a stale `report.json`, a warning when an item-fragment entry
  answers several different calls, C4 accepts a quoted phrase, S6 case-insensitive, S7 skips unit/id fields,
  `memory_ledger.py run --wait-exit`. Bar `2026-11-25.4` for wave 2 (checks only loosened).
- Wave 2: `/home/werg/data/natlang-novel-programs/wave2-20261125/BRIEF.md` (take, build, dry-run, self-check, qualify,
  admit, report; friction log kept; ~190 cards unclaimed).

**Success and failure.** Judged on a drawn sample of wave-2 admissions against wave 1's final grades: success is mean
grades no lower than wave 1's final ones (semantic depth 3-4) with `wrong_expected` on at most one sampled program in
four, at well under wave 1's builder-plus-reviewer inference per admitted program. Failure: a sampled wrong-expected
rate above one in three, or a recurring finding the brief already covers; then the funnel findings change the brief
again before wave 3.
