## 2026-11-25 10:20 Authored trajectories enter expert iteration as a teacher tier (authored-trajectory agent)

- **Why.** The owner (2026-11-25) asked why authored trajectories are not trained directly: "Just have the author write
  the entire execution trajectory to train on and then all we need to do is collect the reasoning in between the
  actions". An admitted invented program's reference run is such a trajectory. Its root actions and the scripted answer
  of every judgment call are authored, and the runtime renders each call's input exactly as the model sees it.
- **Format.** `natlang.authored-trajectory/1` (`scripts/neuralese_data/authored_trajectories.py`): a task row
  (natlang.program/2 with its oracle) plus optional `turns` ({invocation_id, function, messages, tools, target}).
  - Without turns, the task's `curriculum.reference` is the trajectory. `scripts/rl_tasks/reference_episodes.mjs`
    renders it through the collector's own path (`replayReference`, new `onTurn` hook), so iteration, folder
    reducers and decision readouts come out as the runtime issues them.
  - Producer-neutral. The campaign redesign's authored trajectories (deep natlang codebases, natlang-specific calls)
    enter through the same format: either a task row whose reference holds the authored actions, or pre-rendered
    turns.
  - Targets carry no reasoning, and a row with `reasoning_content` is refused.
- **How it enters training.** No parallel mechanism; this extends the existing teacher path.
  - `pool` writes a teacher_gen-layout pool (`manifest.jsonl`, `episodes/<e>/{cases,rollouts}.jsonl`), which
    `sft_sources extract --teacher` reads unchanged.
  - The async driver's round extraction (`prepare_plan`) adds every pool of registry role `ei-authored-teacher` to its
    `teacher-*` campaigns. Opt-out: `async-drive --no-authored-teacher`.
  - The replay re-runs each task under the pin's runtime and oracle. The build then takes the replays as teacher
    episodes, own successes first per the frontier. An empty think block is zero-weight context and the actions are
    the targets.
  - The reasoning between actions comes from the existing fill. `feed` also extracts and replays the pools into the
    WORK `data_nvme:sft-invented-authored`, which is promoted to role `grpo-sd-teacher`, so `filled_reasoning.py
    generate` draws them. Their `filled` units replace the teacher rows (`replaces=teacher`) under the filled build's
    existing weighting.
  - Decision readouts: the authored answer is marked as a reasoned group (`decision_reasoning`, 16 repeats), so the
    replay serves the collector's reasoning samples and the answer request.
- **Continuous.** `invented.py publish` runs `authored_trajectories.py feed` after each batch (opt-out `--no-authored`).
  - The feed takes every admitted program of the train split that no review withheld and that has no export at its
    admitted digest (`ROOT/authored/exported.jsonl`).
  - Each feed writes `ROOT/authored/<stamp>/` and records registry dataset `natlang-sft-invented-authored-<stamp>`
    (role `ei-authored-teacher`).
- **Held separation.** The feed reads only train-split admissions. `pool` refuses any row whose task split is not
  train, and every task `held_eval.training_exclusion_ids` names: held-v3/v2, held-inv (`held-eval-invented`) and every
  `held-eval*` role, with siblings.
- **Fix found on the way (`sft_sources.drifted_success`).** A drifted success whose replay served a reasoned readout's
  repeats (`group-repeat`) was refused, although `exact` already treats those repeats as answered by the matched
  entry. The turn count now compares with `replay_calls`.
  - Effect: drifted teacher episodes with reasoned readouts were silently dropped from every build. That covers
    authored whole programs, whose reference render uses a 16k display budget and so drifts on long arguments.
- **Reaches aei1 at its next driver restart** (the pin must include this commit). The fill takes the WORK at its next
  launch, since a fill unit reads the role at launch.
- **Left out:** `expert_iteration.py cycle` (being replaced by async-drive; its data stage extracts no teacher pools).
- Tests: `tests/neuralese/test_authored_trajectories.py`; the `onTurn` case in
  `ts-host/test/scripted-decision-reply.test.mjs`.

## 2026-11-25 10:40 The std combinators are eval built-ins (semantic-FP strand)

- **Why.** Semantic functional programming (plans/semantic-fp/) needs the model executing a `.nl` function to compose
  its judgments with map/filter/reduce/rank/repair combinators in its own eval. Measured under
  `curriculum.replayReference`: a bare `semanticMap(...)` was `unbound-name`, and an eval `import ... from
  '@natlang/node/std'` loaded the package through the workspace loader, which is a second copy of the runtime with no
  task. The call then failed with "No natlang task is active here".
- **What.** Every eval has `semanticMap`, `semanticFilter`, `semanticPartition`, `semanticReduce`, `semanticMatch`,
  `semanticRank`, `semanticRepair`, `fixedPoint`, `semanticMerge`, `escalate`, `withContext` and `compileRule`, plus
  `proposeAndVerify` and `branchAndSelect` where the call has a folder.
  - They are the platform's own std instance (`runtime/modules.ts stdModule`). Eval reaches it through the shipped
    module registry, so no `native -> std` import edge is added.
  - Each one runs in `currentFrame() ?? call frame`, so `std:<name>` spans and their child calls nest under the call.
  - The eval checker types them as `typeof import('/__natlang__/std').<name>`.
  - An eval import of a combinator lowers to the built-in (`scope-compiler.ts lowerStdImports`). Any other std import
    fails with one sentence naming the built-ins.
  - Discovery is through the scope guide, `read_code(name)` docs and the tool-call redirect. The system prompt, tool
    list and opening line are unchanged.
- **Two fixes found on the way.** Each ships as the default.
  - Eval's functions and inline `nl` are bound to the call's frame, so their calls skipped a combinator's span and
    nested under the call. A decide readout around them was lost too. A span frame now records the call that opened it
    (`Frame.spanOf`), and a bound call started in that span nests under it (`callable.ts startCall`).
  - Combinators pass callbacks JavaScript's `(item, index)`, and a `.nl` function refuses arguments it does not
    declare ("summarize expects 1 arguments, got 2"). `std/collections.ts callback` passes a natlang function only
    the arguments it declares.
  - Not changed: `notes.map(summarize)` in eval still fails the same way (the kernel's arity check,
    `kernel.ts` ~701).
- **Opt-out.** `NATLANG_EVAL_STD=0`.
- **Left out.**
  - The Python folder host (`native/python-sources.ts` PYTHON_NATLANG binds only `nl` and `iterate_on`; Python
    callbacks need per-run proxy lifetimes, as `_Iteration` shows).
  - The workerd core when its consumer does not load `@natlang/core/std` (`core/index.ts` does not import
    `std/index.ts`; `stdModule` then returns nothing and eval offers no combinators).

## 2026-11-25 Program generation redesigned: authored trajectories of semantic functional programs; statistics, not checks (program-inventor strand)

**Owner (2026-11-25):** "why don't we just author entire trajectories directly for the IR without having to run it
through a model? Just have the author write the entire execution trajectory to train on and then all we need to do is
collect the reasoning in between the actions." "We very, very strongly need to limit the amount of crisp TypeScript
code ... a deep code base of purely natural language functions able to call each other ... use a lot of the NatLang
specific functionality ... we need statistics not checks ... feeding analysis back into top of funnel prompting."
"Remember we want to do semantic functional programming." Runtime function synthesis: "It's just built in our ability
to make these nl literals."

**Why.** The exact-checker bar (requirements D1/D5: 100 lines of TypeScript with an algorithm; S4 "one defensible
answer"; ablations, wrong answers, keyword baselines) drove the 13 admitted programs to TypeScript algorithms around
narrow classification leaves (statute-amendment-consolidator: 8 `.ts` files, 6 leaf readers). That is the opposite of
the target shape.

**What changed.**
- `natlang.authored-program/1` (`scripts/rl_tasks/sources/authored_programs.py`, `scripts/rl_tasks/authored_replay.mjs`):
  a builder writes the program, 1-3 literal instances and each instance's whole trajectory (`trajectory.root`: the
  root's turns; `trajectory.calls`: one entry per call below the root, `fn` + `match` fragments, `value` or `turns`).
  The only check: `natlang check`, then the trajectory replays through `curriculum.replayReference` with no model to a
  finished root call, every call answered, no failed action (unless `expected_failures`), types satisfied. An instance
  with an `rl` oracle also becomes an RL task (optional by-product; `invented.py publish` skips admissions without one).
- **Trajectory format for the exporter.** `admit` writes `ROOT/admitted/<slug>/trajectories.jsonl`: one
  `natlang.program/2` case per instance whose `curriculum.reference` is the authored trajectory (children ordered most
  specific first, `fn` as the `You are inside this call: fn(` anchor) and whose `semantics.expected` is the value the
  replay returns. This is the input `scripts/rl_tasks/reference_episodes.mjs` reads (the authored-trajectory exporter
  strand). Only `split: train` rows may be trained: dev/confirmation ideas are the held-inv slice (`admission.json`
  `split`, each case's `split`). Reasoning is left empty for `filled_reasoning.py`.
- **Statistics** (per program in `check`/`stats`, per wave in `wave-report WAVE`): calls by construct, NL composition
  depth (root included), interior functions, TS logic lines vs `.nl` instruction lines, NL calls vs helper calls,
  higher-order uses, combinator uses, recursion and iteration (measure vs NL predicate), decisions, ensures, NL
  literals (created, built from data, calls through them, share of the call tree through them), answer lengths,
  open/structured/closed outputs. Targets (`TARGETS`) are statistics, never gates. The wave report writes
  `REPORT.md`, `report.json` and `EMPHASIS.draft.md`; the coordinator edits the draft into the next wave's
  `EMPHASIS.md`, which `BUILD_BRIEF.md` has every builder read first (the top-of-funnel feedback).
- `applications/program-inventor/BUILD_BRIEF.md` rewritten (program shape, construct inventory with each construct's
  trajectory form, trajectory format, tools, statistics); `requirements.json` is three checks plus nine statistics;
  `REVIEW_BRIEF.md` is a drawn-sample pass grading semantic-FP shape, depth, synthesis and trajectory realism, listing
  bad authored answers and funnel findings. Skill: SKILL.md step 2 (short exact steps in the calling function's eval),
  composition.md "Functions built from data" (NL literals from derived values; a `.nl` function with a function
  result). Worked mechanics example: `/home/werg/data/natlang-novel-programs/authored-examples/thread-digest/`.
- Wave 2's 12 claims released as `abandoned` (the cards are free again).

**Found on the way.** The std combinators are not reachable from a `.nl` call's eval (OPEN_ITEMS "std combinators are
not in eval's scope"); a std-in-eval agent is adding them as eval built-ins. Until it lands, trajectories map with
`Promise.all`, reduce with `for...of` and loop with `iterateOn`.

**Success / failure.** Success: wave statistics move toward the targets wave over wave (crisp share <= 0.15, NL depth
>= 4, >= 6 construct kinds, >= 1 data-built NL literal per instance) at well under the exact-checker bar's inference
per admitted program, and the exporter renders the admitted trajectories into rows. Failure: drawn-sample reviews find
bad authored answers in more than one call in ten, or statistics flat across two waves; then the brief changes.

## 2026-11-25 13:20 Memory ledger measures claims outside the allocator lock; waiters poll every 5 s (ops strand)

**Observation.** ~13:00: eight 2 GB `pauth-aw2-*-check-*` jobs (reserve 3 GB) waited 6-8 min with 22 GB headroom and
an empty `cannot_fit`; a builder reported ~40 min of ledger queueing in a 1 h 50 min build.

**Cause.** Neither the reserve, learned peaks (every `pauth-*-check-N` is its own family, peaks <= 1 GB) nor backfill
explains it: the jobs fit. Every ledger transaction measured all claims under the exclusive flock (`live_claims`:
per unit `systemctl show` twice, `docker inspect` up to twice, `smaps_rollup` per process: 225 reads at 22 ms). One
pass took 6.6-9.5 s for 15 claims; the guard repeated it every 1 s (`--interval 1`, 12 h CPU in 25 h), and each
waiting `run` every 30 s. A fresh flock waited 62 s; admissions ran ~1 per 8-10 s machine-wide (243 in 103 min), so a
waiter got one try per minute and only the queue head (or a spare backfill) could start on it.

**Fix (default, opt-out `NATLANG_LEDGER_SHARED_USAGE=0`).** `shared_usage` measures outside the allocator lock into a
cache (`memory-ledger.json.usage.json`) reused for 15 s by `run`, `status` and `admissible`; the guard measures afresh
each cycle and refreshes it. Under the lock only claims admitted after the measurement are measured; a finished claim is
released only when measured >30 s after its admission. Waiters poll every 5 s (`RUN_POLL_SECONDS`); a waiter does not
wait more than 15 s on another's measurement; `status` never waits. `family_peaks` (36k one-off families, 1.6 of the
1.9 MB file) keeps the 4000 most recently updated. Admitted events record `waited_s`. GB10 accounting, the 15 GB
default reserve, ramp reservations and priorities are unchanged. After the guard restart a flock waits 0 s.

  unchanged: it is the owner-endorsed diversity rule, and a lineage-cumulative family share would change what
  diversity means. This is listed as a lever.

**Changes (default on, each with an opt-out; enter at the driver's next restart).**
1. **The fills fill the campaigns first and skip trained episodes** (`expert_iteration.Cycle.fill_command`,
   `filled_reasoning generate --skip-trained BUILD`). The loop's sources WORK is a `--prefer-work`: it comes after the

   `--no-fill-campaigns`.

   --campaign-work WORK...`, `FillPending`). A campaign episode younger than 12 h (its `rollouts.jsonl` mtime) that
   the fill has not attempted is not admitted raw (funnel `fill_pending`). It trains as its fill in a later round, or
   raw once it is older than 12 h or the fill declined it. Opt-out: `--defer-unfilled-hours 0`.

   `sft_sources.drop_solved_own`). The frontier tier decides where the frontier measured the task. Otherwise the
   recorded rate decides, at >= 0.75 over >= 2 samples (fixed rates: the 5312e06c3 zero-call rule). Funnel:
   `own_task_solved`. Opt-out: `--own-solved-anchor 1` (the old light anchor).
4. **Round size: larger and fewer** (`AsyncRoundDriver.supply_wait`, `mix_supply`). The rule: a round trains once its
   mix holds >= 5M weighted target tokens outside the own successes (`--min-new-tokens`). Every unit counted there is
   new, because the no-repetition rule drops anything an earlier build trained. A shorter build waits 45 min
   (`--supply-recheck-minutes`) while collection, teacher campaign and fills run on, then reruns data and build. After
   12 h from the first short build (`--max-supply-wait-hours`) it trains anyway. Each pass is in
   `rNNNN/stages/supply.json`, and the decision goes to round.json (`supply`) and the drive log. Opt-out:
   `--min-new-tokens 0`.
5. **A fixed held-like validation set** (`sft_sources build --fixed-val ROOT/val-fixed`, `FixedVal`). It holds one
   verified success on each of up to 40 own and 40 teacher tasks from held-v3's families. These are never a held task
   or a source-group sibling (the build's candidates already exclude the held closure) and never a task an earlier
   build trained. The tasks are chosen once by hash and then frozen (`tasks.json`, `val-fixed-{own,teacher}.pkl`). No
   build that names the set trains those tasks or their Neuralese variants (core candidates, and aux units through the
   held closure). The learner scores the sets before step 1 and after its last step, beside the round's own left-over
   sets (`sft_env`: VAL and `--val-chains`). The driver records before, after and change per set in round.json
   (`validation`) and the drive log (`round_validation`). Opt-out: `--no-fixed-val`. This replaces the per-round
   `val-teacher` sets. r4-r7's moved 1-4% at loss 0.003-0.03, and from r9 on they were empty, because the
   no-repetition rule leaves no untrained left-overs.

**Expected supply (from the measured rates).** The campaigns score about 150-200 successes an hour. If the fill keeps
up, each one carries ~2K filled tokens instead of ~0.9K raw, so roughly 0.3-0.4M new tokens an hour. That is 5M in
about 13-17 h. Rounds therefore wait up to the 12 h cap unless teacher throughput or fill capacity rises. Also, once:
2,175 untrained campaign successes (~4M once filled) and the 28 authored programs (role `ei-authored-teacher`, extracted
since adf901c52).

## 2026-11-25 15:40 Compaction captures splice on the fork and the page (capture-kind strand)

The Python engines store a reply captured in its own context as `producer_kind` 'capture' and splice it when read
(15:00 "Learned compaction on by default", item 2). The managed llama-server and the page now do the same:
- Fork b536c7379 (`neuralese`): 'capture' is valid native-state metadata; it splices as stored (`exact-native-state`)
  unless `NATLANG_NEURALESE_CAPTURE_IN_CONTEXT=1` (read per request); a chat completion's
  `x_natlang_producer_kind: "capture"` stamps the spans that request produces (any value but "capture"/"span" refused);
  `/v1/neuralese/info` lists `native.producer-kind.capture`. Release natlang-b12094 (dispatched, quick archives and
  the page's wllama); natlang pinned to it with `update_llama_runtime.mjs --fork` (page build vendored from the same
  release), `llama-fork-source.ts` to b536c7379.
- Client: `grammarCapture` sends the field for a reply capture (never for a write, which stays 'span' and is read in
  context) when the server lists the capability, and refuses a stored kind other than 'capture'. The ts-host stores
  refused 'capture' (`validateNativeState` knew only text/span), so a Python-engine capture archived to a ts-host store
  failed; fixed in the same commit.
- Checks: fork unit tests `test_natlang_native_state.py` 7/7 on the 8e634a0f Q8_0 GGUF (CPU build); live
  `check_llama_native_state_protocol.py` passes with the new capture leg: stored kind 'capture', id equal to the
  reference codec's (`serve/store.native_state_id`) for the same tensors with that kind, consumer receipt
  `exact-native-state`. Content ids match the Python engines' rule; the literal ids differ across engines only through
  the tensors (Q8_0 vs BF16). ts-host targeted tests pass. The page has no capture of its own yet (ENGINE_PARITY
  text-write table), so it gains only the read rule and validation; no page smoke ran.

## 2026-11-25 15:22 Authored trajectories carry learned compaction and Neuralese values (authored-neuralese strand)

- **Why.** A builder reported that BUILD_BRIEF has no Neuralese row and `check` cannot author a Neuralese value. Owner
  direction: Neuralese compaction is the intended runtime design, and learned compaction (`compaction: nl`) is on by
  default as of today (model-facing `learned-compaction`). Authored trajectories must teach what collection rollouts
  contain.
- **Before.** `curriculum.replayReference` ran with no Neuralese runtime and a driver without `neuralese: true`.
  - A `Neuralese<string>` result failed with `NeuraleseNoWriterError` ("plain-text Neuralese<string> cannot be
    written"), so `check` could not finish such a program.
  - A long value kept the crisp cut: `compactRef` needs `neuralese.capture` and a Neuralese driver, so there was no
    operator call and no state. The trajectory therefore differed from collection.
  - The `sft_sources replay` of authored teacher episodes ran over the remote HTTP default with teacher-text emulation.
    A Neuralese value would have rendered as `[[teacher-text Neuralese id=… body=…]]`, which is not the serving form.
- **Now (one mechanism, `ts-host/src/model/in-context-neuralese.ts`).** It is a scripted transport for the engines'
  default read (`in-context-text`: a state written in its producing context is read as its tokens in place, with no
  markers). It has an in-memory store, a `capture` (operator replies, `compact_history` notes) and a `port` (typed
  `Neuralese<T>` writes) that keep each state's text. Its `wrap(driver)` gives every request, `decide` included, the
  consumer's messages with each state's text in place, and adds the engines' `in-context-text` import receipts. Under
  replay the runtime's own paths run (`compactRef` → `operatorWrite` → capture; `writeNeuraleseText` → port), the same
  code as in collection. The compaction setting is the agent's own (env, model-facing), as in collection.
  - `replayReference(..., { neuralese })`. In `referenceDriver`, an operator request (`<call>#operator-<n>`) is a call
    of `view` (`OPERATOR_CALL`): it is matched by its opening (instructions and value), and its entry's `value` is the
    reply text.
  - `authored_replay.mjs` (`check`/`dump`/`admit`) and `reference_episodes.mjs` (render) use it by default (opt-out
    `--no-neuralese`). An operator call with no entry is `NO ENTRY … view` and gets a placeholder summary. The
    statistics count `operator_calls` (construct `compaction`).
  - `authored_trajectories.py`: an operator turn is its own per-call chain (function `view`, target = the summary) and
    never a reasoned-readout group. Consumer turns carry the summary in place (plain text, as the learner sees an
    in-context read).
  - Replay for training: `sft_sources.replay_episode` marks authored episodes (teacher provider `authored`) with entry
    `in_context_neuralese`. `run_bonsai_queue` passes `--in-context-neuralese` (in place of teacher-text emulation),
    and the collector (`inContextNeuralese`) wraps its driver and records the inlined messages. The replay therefore
    renders what the authored render did.
  - BUILD_BRIEF: construct rows "Long value (learned compaction)" and "Neuralese value", plus `check`'s behaviour.
- **Replay of a sample program** (`authored_programs.py check`/`dump`, `authored_trajectories.py render` on a
  three-function program with a 15,890-character log input and a `Neuralese<string>` gist): the root's and the
  receiving leaf's listings each made a `view` call. The root's had no entry, so it was listed as `NO ENTRY ... view`
  with suggested fragment `The call that receives this argument as log (string) answers: ...`. The leaf's listing showed
  `log: string = <summary>  // view of the value; log holds all of it`. The consumer of the gist showed
  `gist: Neuralese<string> = <gist text>`, and no request carried a sentinel. The rendered rows came out as
  [root, view (target: the summary, no tools), gistLog, writeBriefing].
- **Interplay.** The operator-thinking strand renders operator calls with `thinking: false`. Authored operator turns
  carry no reasoning, so they already match operator rows (empty think block, then the summary).
- **Left out.**
  - Other scripted replays (`verifyCases`, handoffs `build-handoffs.mjs`, native-forced replay) keep no Neuralese
    transport. Their recorded turns have no operator replies to serve, so a run with operators would only drift.
  - In-page wllama, the engines and the learners are unchanged: this mirrors the engines' existing default read and
    adds no serving feature.
  - A state inside tool-call `arguments` is inlined JSON-escaped, so the arguments stay valid JSON. The engine feeds
    the raw tokens there. No authored path produces this today.
- Tests: `ts-host/test/authored-in-context-neuralese.test.mjs` (2),
  `tests/neuralese/test_authored_trajectories.py::test_an_operator_call_is_its_own_turn_not_a_readout_...`,
  `tests/test_bonsai_queue.py::test_entry_in_context_neuralese_replaces_the_text_transport`. The ledger units
  `authnz-tests-1` and `authnz-tests-2` ran them, plus `test_authored_programs.py`. In `test_bonsai_queue.py`, four
